In addition to premium, fees may be charged on your policy . We may charge fees for installment payments, late payments, and other transactions. - 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or

and its custom parts or equipment , resulting from collision .

In addition, we will pay the reasonable cost to replace any child safety seat damaged in an accident to which this coverage applies.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COMPREHENSIVE COVERAGE

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to a:

- 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or
2. non-owned auto ;

and its custom parts or equipment , that is not caused by collision .

## A loss not caused by collision includes:

- 1 . contact with an animal (including a bird);
2. explosion or earthquake;
3. fire;
4. malicious mischief or vandalism;
5. missiles or falling objects;
6. riot or civil commotion;
- 7 . theft or larceny;
8. windstorm, hail, water or flood; or
9. breakage of glass not caused by collision .

## In addition, we will pay for:

- 1 . reasonable transportation expenses incurred by you if a covered auto is stolen; and
2. loss of use damages that you are legally liable to pay if a non-owned auto is stolen. A combined maximum of $900, not exceeding $30 per day, will apply to these additional benefits. The additional benefit for transportation expenses will not apply if you purchased Rental Reimbursement Coverage for the stolen covered auto .

Coverage for transportation expenses and loss of use damages begins 48 hours after you report the theft to us and ends the earliest of:

- 1 . when the auto has been recovered and returned to you or its owner;
2. when the auto has been recovered and repaired;
3. when the auto has been replaced;
4. 72 hours after we make an offer to settle the loss if the auto is deemed by us to be a total loss; or

5. if the loss is theft of a rented non-owned auto , 30 days after loss of use begins on the loss.

We must receive written proof of transportation expenses and loss of use damages.

This coverage applies in addition to any coverage automatically provided for custom parts or equipment under Comprehensive Coverage or Collision Coverage.

This coverage is limited to the each day limit shown on the declarations page for a maximum of 30 days.

## CHANGES

This policy contract, your insurance application (which is made a part of this policy as if attached hereto), the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy issued by us , contain all the agreements between you and us .   Subject to the following, the terms of this policy may not be changed or waived except by an endorsement issued by us .

If this information is determined by us to be incorrect, incomplete, or if it changes during the policy period, you agree that we may adjust your policy information and premium accordingly. Changes that may result in a premium adjustment are contained in our rates and rules. These include, but are not limited to, you , a relative , or a rated resident obtaining a driver's license or operator's permit, or changes in:

- 1 . the number, type or use classification of covered autos ;

4. the residents in your household;
5. an operator's marital status;
6. your mailing address and your residence address;

8. coverage, deductibles, or limits of liability; or
9. rating territory or discount eligibility .

The coverage provided in your policy may be changed only by the issuance of a new policy or an endorsement by us .  However, if during the policy period we broaden any coverage afforded under the current edition of your policy without additional premium charge, that change will automatically apply to your policy as of the date the coverage change is implemented in your state.

If you ask us to delete a vehicle from this policy , no coverage will apply to that vehicle as of the date and time you ask us to delete it.

You must promptly report to us all changes, including additions and deletions, in policy information. This includes, but is not limited to, changes in:

## TERMS OF POLICY CONFORMED TO STATUTES

## LIMITS OF LIABILITY

The limit of liability shown on the declarations page for  Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage is the most we will pay regardless of the number of:

The 'each person' limit of liability includes the total of all claims made for bodily injury to an insured person and all claims of others derived from such bodily injury , including, but not limited to, emotional injury or mental anguish resulting from the bodily injury of another or from witnessing the bodily injury to another, loss of society , loss of companionship, loss of services, loss of consortium, and wrongful death.

If  the declarations  page shows  that  'combined  single  limit'  or  'CSL '  applies,  the amount shown is the most we will pay for the total of all damages resulting from any one accident. - 1 . paid because of bodily injury by or on behalf of any persons or organizations that may be legally responsible;

- a. workers' compensation law; or

If there is other applicable uninsured or underinsured motorist coverage, the total of the applicable limits of liability available under all uninsured or underinsured motorist coverages combined will be reduced by all sums:

No one will be entitled to duplicate payments for the same elements of damages.

## LIMITS OF LIABILITY

The limit of liability shown on the declarations page for liability coverage is the most we will pay regardless of the number of:

- 1 . claims made;
2. covered autos ;
3. insured persons ;
4. lawsuits brought;
5. vehicles involved in the accident; or
6. premiums paid.

## If your declarations page shows a split limit:

- 1 . the amount shown for 'each person' is the most we will pay for all damages due to bodily injury to one person resulting from any one accident;
2. subject to the 'each person' limit, the amount shown for 'each accident' is the most we will pay for all damages due to bodily injury sustained by two or more persons in any one accident; and
3. the amount shown for 'property damage' is the most we will pay for the total of all property damage resulting from any one accident.

The 'each person' limit of liability applies to the total of all claims made for bodily injury to a person and all claims of others derived from such bodily injury , including, but not

limited to, emotional injury or mental anguish resulting from the bodily injury of another or from witnessing the bodily injury to another, loss of society , loss of companionship, loss of services, loss of consortium, and wrongful death.

If  the declarations  page shows  that  'combined  single  limit'  or  'CSL '  applies,  the amount shown is the most we will pay for the total of all damages resulting from any one accident. However, without changing this limit of liability , we will comply with any law that requires us to provide any separate limits.

## MAINE AUTO POLICY

## INSURING AGREEMENT

In return for your payment of the premium, we agree to insure you subject to all the terms, conditions and limitations of this policy . We will insure you for the coverages and the limits of liability shown on this policy's declarations page . Your policy consists of the policy contract, your insurance application, the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy .

## GENERAL DEFINITIONS

The following definitions apply throughout the policy . Defined terms are printed in boldface type and have the same meaning whether in the singular, plural, or any other form.

- 1 . ' Additional auto ' means an auto you become the owner of during the policy period that does not permanently replace an auto shown on the declarations page
- if:
- a. we insure all other autos you own;
- b. the additional auto is not covered by any other insurance policy;
- c. you notify us within 30 days of becoming the owner of the additional auto ; and
- d. you pay any additional premium due.

An additional auto will have the broadest coverage we provide for any auto shown on the declarations page .  If you ask us to insure an additional auto more than 30 days after you become the owner, any coverage we provide will begin at the time you request coverage.

Unless both parties agree otherwise, arbitration will take place in the county in which the insured person resides. Local rules of procedure and evidence will apply .

A decision agreed to by two of the arbitrators will be binding with respect to a determination of:

The arbitrators will have no authority to award an amount in excess of the limit of liability .

We and an insured person may agree to an alternate form of arbitration.

## PART IV-DAMAGE TO A VEHICLE

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COLLISION COVERAGE

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to a:

- 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or
2. non-owned auto ;

and its custom parts or equipment , resulting from collision .

In addition, we will pay the reasonable cost to replace any child safety seat damaged in an accident to which this coverage applies.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COMPREHENSIVE COVERAGE

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to a:

- 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or
2. non-owned auto ;

and its custom parts or equipment , that is not caused by collision .

## A loss not caused by collision includes:

- 1 . contact with an animal (including a bird);
2. explosion or earthquake;
3. fire;
4. malicious mischief or vandalism;
5. missiles or falling objects;
6. riot or civil commotion;
- 7 . theft or larceny;
8. windstorm, hail, water or flood; or
9. breakage of glass not caused by collision .

## In addition, we will pay for:

- 1 . reasonable transportation expenses incurred by you if a covered auto is stolen; and
2. loss of use damages that you are legally liable to pay if a non-owned auto is stolen. A combined maximum of $900, not exceeding $30 per day, will apply to these additional benefits. The additional benefit for transportation expenses will not apply if you purchased Rental Reimbursement Coverage for the stolen covered auto .

Coverage for transportation expenses and loss of use damages begins 48 hours after you report the theft to us and ends the earliest of:

- 1 . when the auto has been recovered and returned to you or its owner;
2. when the auto has been recovered and repaired;
3. when the auto has been replaced;
4. 72 hours after we make an offer to settle the loss if the auto is deemed by us to be a total loss; or

5. if the loss is theft of a rented non-owned auto , 30 days after loss of use begins on the loss.

We must receive written proof of transportation expenses and loss of use damages.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-ADDITIONAL CUSTOM PARTS OR EQUIPMENT COVERAGE

We will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to custom parts or equipment on a covered auto for which this coverage has been purchased. This coverage applies only if you have purchased both Comprehensive Coverage and Collision Coverage for that covered auto and the loss is covered under one of those coverages. This coverage applies in addition to any coverage automatically provided for custom parts or equipment under Comprehensive Coverage or Collision Coverage.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-RENTAL REIMBURSEMENT COVERAGE

We will reimburse rental charges incurred when you rent an auto from a rental agency or auto repair shop due to a loss to a covered auto for which Rental Reimbursement Coverage has been purchased. This coverage applies only if you have purchased both Comprehensive Coverage and Collision Coverage for that covered auto and the loss is covered under one of those coverages.

Additional fees or charges for insurance, damage waivers, optional equipment, fuel, or accessories are not covered.

This coverage is limited to the each day limit shown on the declarations page for a maximum of 30 days.

If  Rental Reimbursement Coverage applies, no other coverage under this policy for rental expenses will apply .

## Rental charges will be reimbursed beginning:

- 1 . when the covered auto cannot be driven due to a loss; or
2. if the covered auto can be driven, when you deliver the covered auto to an auto repair shop or one of our Service Centers for repairs due to the loss; and ending the earliest of:
- 1 . when the covered auto has been returned to you ;
2. when the covered auto has been repaired;
3. when the covered auto has been replaced;
4. 72 hours after we make an offer to settle the loss if the covered auto is deemed by us to be a total loss; or
5. when you incur 30 days worth of rental charges.

You must provide us written proof of your rental charges to be reimbursed.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-PET INJURY COVERAGE

If you have purchased Collision coverage for at least one covered auto under your policy , and if your pet sustains injury or death while inside a covered auto or nonowned auto at the time of a loss covered under Collision or Comprehensive coverage, we will provide:

- 1 . up to $1,000 for reasonable and customary veterinary fees incurred by you , a relative , or a rated resident if your pet is injured in, or as a direct result of, the covered loss; or
2. a $1,000 death benefit if your pet dies in, or as a direct result of, the covered loss, less any payment we made toward veterinary expenses for your pet .

In the event of a covered loss due to the theft of a covered auto or non-owned auto , we will provide the death benefit provided your pet is inside that auto at the time of the theft and your pet is not recovered.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COLLISION COVERAGE

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to a:

- 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or
2. non-owned auto ;

and its custom parts or equipment , resulting from collision .

In addition, we will pay the reasonable cost to replace any child safety seat damaged in an accident to which this coverage applies.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COMPREHENSIVE COVERAGE

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to a:

- 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or
2. non-owned auto ;

and its custom parts or equipment , that is not caused by collision .

## A loss not caused by collision includes:

- 1 . contact with an animal (including a bird);
2. explosion or earthquake;
3. fire;
4. malicious mischief or vandalism;
5. missiles or falling objects;
6. riot or civil commotion;
- 7 . theft or larceny;
8. windstorm, hail, water or flood; or
9. breakage of glass not caused by collision .

## In addition, we will pay for:

- 1 . reasonable transportation expenses incurred by you if a covered auto is stolen; and
2. loss of use damages that you are legally liable to pay if a non-owned auto is stolen. A combined maximum of $900, not exceeding $30 per day, will apply to these additional benefits. The additional benefit for transportation expenses will not apply if you purchased Rental Reimbursement Coverage for the stolen covered auto .

Coverage for transportation expenses and loss of use damages begins 48 hours after you report the theft to us and ends the earliest of:

- 1 . when the auto has been recovered and returned to you or its owner;
2. when the auto has been recovered and repaired;
3. when the auto has been replaced;
4. 72 hours after we make an offer to settle the loss if the auto is deemed by us to be a total loss; or

5. if the loss is theft of a rented non-owned auto , 30 days after loss of use begins on the loss.

We must receive written proof of transportation expenses and loss of use damages.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-ADDITIONAL CUSTOM PARTS OR EQUIPMENT COVERAGE

We will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to custom parts or equipment on a covered auto for which this coverage has been purchased. This coverage applies only if you have purchased both Comprehensive Coverage and Collision Coverage for that covered auto and the loss is covered under one of those coverages. This coverage applies in addition to any coverage automatically provided for custom parts or equipment under Comprehensive Coverage or Collision Coverage.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-RENTAL REIMBURSEMENT COVERAGE

We will reimburse rental charges incurred when you rent an auto from a rental agency or auto repair shop due to a loss to a covered auto for which Rental Reimbursement Coverage has been purchased. This coverage applies only if you have purchased both Comprehensive Coverage and Collision Coverage for that covered auto and the loss is covered under one of those coverages.

Additional fees or charges for insurance, damage waivers, optional equipment, fuel, or accessories are not covered.

This coverage is limited to the each day limit shown on the declarations page for a maximum of 30 days.

If  Rental Reimbursement Coverage applies, no other coverage under this policy for rental expenses will apply .

- 1 . when the covered auto cannot be driven due to a loss; or

## LIMITS OF LIABILITY

The limit of liability shown on the declarations page for  Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage is the most we will pay regardless of the number of:

The 'each person' limit of liability includes the total of all claims made for bodily injury to an insured person and all claims of others derived from such bodily injury , including, but not limited to, emotional injury or mental anguish resulting from the bodily injury of another or from witnessing the bodily injury to another, loss of society , loss of companionship, loss of services, loss of consortium, and wrongful death.

## INSURING AGREEMENT

In return for your payment of the premium, we agree to insure you subject to all the terms, conditions and limitations of this policy . We will insure you for the coverages and the limits of liability shown on this policy's declarations page . Your policy consists of the policy contract, your insurance application, the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy .

The following definitions apply throughout the policy . Defined terms are printed in boldface type and have the same meaning whether in the singular, plural, or any other form.

- d. you pay any additional premium due.

An additional auto will have the broadest coverage we provide for any auto shown on the declarations page .  If you ask us to insure an additional auto more than 30 days after you become the owner, any coverage we provide will begin at the time you request coverage.

60|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY refers to the use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation, including activities conducted through transportation network companies (TNCs) such as ride-hailing platforms. The exclusion applies from the moment a user logs on to the TNC’s system until they log out, encompassing all time spent en route to pick up passengers, transporting them, or waiting for a ride request. This includes both the actual passenger transport and any associated travel time between pickups and drop-offs.

RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is distinct from the shared-expense carpool exception, which allows limited coverage for non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements among passengers. In contrast, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY involves compensation, meaning the driver receives payment for transporting others, and thus does not qualify for the carpool exception. The policy clearly excludes coverage for any use of a covered auto in connection with commercial ride-sharing services, whether the driver is operating as an independent contractor or under a formal TNC agreement.

The exclusion applies broadly to all forms of compensated passenger transportation, including but not limited to rides provided via smartphone applications, dispatch services, or other digital platforms. This includes scenarios where the vehicle is used to transport persons or property for payment, even if the driver is not formally employed by the TNC. The exclusion remains in effect throughout the entire duration of the ride-sharing activity, from the initial login to the final logout, ensuring that no part of the activity is covered under the policy.

In summary, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is a defined exclusion under the policy, covering any use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation through a transportation network company. It includes all phases of the service—logging in, traveling to pick up passengers, transporting them, and returning to service—regardless of whether the driver is actively matched with a passenger. This exclusion is absolute and does not extend to the shared-expense carpool exception, which only applies to non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements. 8|Policy Period and Related Insurance Factors|"# Policy Period and Related Insurance Factors

The community centers on the POLICY PERIOD, which defines the active duration of an insurance policy and serves as the temporal anchor for all related entities. Key entities such as the INSURANCE APPLICATION, INCEPTION, and various personal and geographic factors (e.g., RESIDENCE ADDRESS, RATING TERRITORY, DRIVER'S LICENSE STATUS) are dynamically linked to the POLICY PERIOD through relationships that govern coverage, premium adjustments, and reporting obligations. These relationships establish a structured framework where changes during the policy period can trigger compliance actions, financial impacts, or coverage modifications.

## The POLICY PERIOD as the central temporal framework

The POLICY PERIOD is the foundational entity in this community, defining the exact start and end dates during which insurance coverage is active. It serves as the temporal boundary for all policy obligations, with events occurring outside this window typically excluded from coverage regardless of claim timing. The declarations page formally records these dates, ensuring clarity for both the policyholder and insurer. The POLICY PERIOD is not automatically extended and requires explicit amendment or renewal to continue coverage. Its precise definition is critical for maintaining continuous protection and avoiding coverage gaps. [Data: Entities (276); Relationships (396, 450, 442, 443, 444, +more)]

## The INSURANCE APPLICATION as the foundational document

The INSURANCE APPLICATION is a legally binding document that forms the basis of the policy and is incorporated into the contract. It contains essential information used to determine initial premium rates and coverage terms. The application's data directly influences the policy's structure and is referenced throughout the policy lifecycle. Its integration into the policy ensures that underwriting decisions are traceable and consistent with the final contract. Changes to the application after issuance may require endorsements or adjustments, but the original application remains a key reference point. [Data: Entities (321); Relationships (418)]

## Dynamic factors affecting premium and coverage during the policy period

Several personal and geographic factors are directly tied to the POLICY PERIOD and can trigger premium adjustments or reporting requirements if changed. These include the PRINCIPAL GARAGING ADDRESS, COVERAGE CLASSIFICATION, DRIVER'S LICENSE STATUS, OPERATOR'S MARITAL STATUS, RESIDENCE ADDRESS, MAILING ADDRESS, RATING TERRITORY, DISCOUNT ELIGIBILITY, PERSON OF LEGAL DRIVING AGE, HOUSEHOLD RESIDENT, and COVERED PERSON. For example, changing the primary garaging address of a covered vehicle may result in a premium adjustment, as it affects risk exposure. Similarly, a change in marital status or household composition may alter discount eligibility and premium calculations. These relationships highlight the ongoing nature of policy management during the policy period. [Data: Entities (334, 335, 336, 337, 338, 339, 340, 341, 352, 353, 354); Relationships (442, 443, 444, 445, 446, 447, 448, 449, 451, 452, 453, +more)]

## The role of INCEPTION in initiating coverage

INCEPTION marks the official start date of the policy, after which coverage becomes active and any changes made by the policyholder are subject to the terms of the policy. This date is critical because it determines when the insurer’s obligations begin and when the policy period officially commences. The relationship between the POLICY PERIOD and INCEPTION is direct and foundational, as the policy period begins precisely at inception. Any events occurring before this date are not covered, even if the application was submitted earlier. This ensures that coverage is only active during the defined window and prevents retroactive claims. [Data: Entities (342); Relationships (450)]

## Geographic and territorial constraints on coverage

The POLICY PERIOD is explicitly tied to a defined TERRITORY, which includes the U.S., Canada, or while being transported between ports. This geographic limitation ensures that coverage applies only within specified regions, and any activity outside these areas may fall outside the scope of protection. The RATING TERRITORY, which is used to determine premium rates, may also change during the policy period, potentially leading to a premium adjustment. These geographic factors are critical in assessing risk and ensuring that coverage aligns with the policyholder’s actual location and travel patterns. [Data: Entities (315, 340); Relationships (396, 448)]

## Reporting obligations triggered by changes during the policy period

The policyholder is required to report changes to key personal and household factors during the policy period, including changes in residence address, mailing address, household residents, or the presence of a person of legal driving age. These changes may affect coverage, premium, or discount eligibility and must be disclosed to maintain policy integrity. Failure to report such changes can result in coverage denial or premium adjustments. The relationships between the POLICY PERIOD and entities like RESIDENCE ADDRESS, HOUSEHOLD RESIDENT, and PERSON OF LEGAL DRIVING AGE emphasize the ongoing nature of policy compliance. [Data: Entities (338, 339, 353, 352); Relationships (446, 447, 451, 452)]

## The impact of driver and household status on policy terms

Changes in driver or household status—such as obtaining a driver’s license, changing marital status, or adding a new household resident—can directly affect the policy’s terms. For instance, a new driver of legal age in the household may increase risk exposure and lead to higher premiums. Similarly, a change in marital status may alter discount eligibility or coverage needs. These dynamic factors are continuously monitored during the policy period, and their impact is governed by the policy’s terms. The relationships between the POLICY PERIOD and DRIVER'S LICENSE STATUS, OPERATOR'S MARITAL STATUS, and HOUSEHOLD RESIDENT reflect the adaptive nature of insurance policies. [Data: Entities (336, 337, 353); Relationships (444, 445, 452)]

## Coverage and protection for covered persons

The COVERED PERSON is an individual protected under the policy, including the named insured and others such as family members or authorized drivers. Their presence and status during the policy period directly influence coverage and premium calculations. Any changes in the identity or status of a covered person must be reported and may result in adjustments to the policy. The relationship between the POLICY PERIOD and COVERED PERSON ensures that protection is active only for those legally recognized as covered during the defined time frame. [Data: Entities (354); Relationships (453)]"

- a. The most we will pay for all damages in any one loss is a total of $1,000 regardless of the number of dogs or cats involved.
- b. If your pet dies in, or as a direct result of, a covered loss, we will provide a death benefit of $1,000, less any payment we made toward veterinary expenses for your pet .
- c. No deductible shall apply to this coverage.

## PAYMENT OF LOSS

We may, at our option:

- 1 . pay for the loss in money; or
2. repair or replace the damaged or stolen property.

At our expense, we may return any recovered stolen property to you or to the address shown on the declarations page , with payment for any damage resulting from the theft. We may keep all or part of the property at the agreed or appraised value.

We may settle any loss with you or the owner or lienholder of the property .

## NO BENEFIT TO BAILEE

Coverage under this Part IV will not directly or indirectly benefit any carrier or other bailee for hire.

## LOSS PAYABLE CLAUSE

Payment under this Part IV for a loss to a covered auto will be made according to your interest and the interest of any lienholder shown on the declarations page or designated by you .  At our option, payment may be made to both jointly, or to either separately. However, if the covered auto is not a total loss, we may make payment to you and the repairer of the auto .

The lienholder's interest will not be protected:

- 1 . where fraud, misrepresentation, material omission, or intentional damage resulting in a denial of coverage by us has been committed by or at the direction of you or any person seeking coverage; or
2. where the loss is otherwise not covered under the terms of this policy .

If this policy is cancelled, nonrenewed or voided, the interest of any lienholder under this agreement will also terminate.

## OTHER SOURCES OF RECOVERY

If other sources of recovery also cover the loss, we will pay only our share of the loss. Our share is the proportion that our limit of liability bears to the total of all applicable

limits. However, any insurance we provide for a non-owned auto , or trailer not shown on the declarations page , will be excess over any other collectible source of recovery including, but not limited to:

- 1 . any coverage provided by the owner of the non-owned auto or trailer ;
2. any other applicable physical damage insurance; and
3. any other source of recovery applicable to the loss.

## APPRAISAL

If we cannot agree with you on the amount of a loss, then we or you may demand an appraisal of the loss. Within 30 days of any demand for an appraisal, each party shall appoint a competent appraiser and shall notify the other party of that appraiser's identity . The appraisers will determine the amount of loss. If they fail to agree, the disagreement will be submitted to a qualified umpire chosen by the appraisers. If the two appraisers are unable to agree upon an umpire within 15 days, we or you may request that a judge of a court of record, in the county where you reside, select an umpire. All other expenses of the appraisal, including payment of the umpire if one is selected, will be shared equally between us and you .   Neither we nor you waive any rights under this policy by agreeing to an appraisal.

8|Policy Period and Related Insurance Factors|"# Policy Period and Related Insurance Factors

The community centers on the POLICY PERIOD, which defines the active duration of an insurance policy and serves as the temporal anchor for all related entities. Key entities such as the INSURANCE APPLICATION, INCEPTION, and various personal and geographic factors (e.g., RESIDENCE ADDRESS, RATING TERRITORY, DRIVER'S LICENSE STATUS) are dynamically linked to the POLICY PERIOD through relationships that govern coverage, premium adjustments, and reporting obligations. These relationships establish a structured framework where changes during the policy period can trigger compliance actions, financial impacts, or coverage modifications.

## The POLICY PERIOD as the central temporal framework

The POLICY PERIOD is the foundational entity in this community, defining the exact start and end dates during which insurance coverage is active. It serves as the temporal boundary for all policy obligations, with events occurring outside this window typically excluded from coverage regardless of claim timing. The declarations page formally records these dates, ensuring clarity for both the policyholder and insurer. The POLICY PERIOD is not automatically extended and requires explicit amendment or renewal to continue coverage. Its precise definition is critical for maintaining continuous protection and avoiding coverage gaps. [Data: Entities (276); Relationships (396, 450, 442, 443, 444, +more)]

## The INSURANCE APPLICATION as the foundational document

The INSURANCE APPLICATION is a legally binding document that forms the basis of the policy and is incorporated into the contract. It contains essential information used to determine initial premium rates and coverage terms. The application's data directly influences the policy's structure and is referenced throughout the policy lifecycle. Its integration into the policy ensures that underwriting decisions are traceable and consistent with the final contract. Changes to the application after issuance may require endorsements or adjustments, but the original application remains a key reference point. [Data: Entities (321); Relationships (418)]

## Dynamic factors affecting premium and coverage during the policy period

Several personal and geographic factors are directly tied to the POLICY PERIOD and can trigger premium adjustments or reporting requirements if changed. These include the PRINCIPAL GARAGING ADDRESS, COVERAGE CLASSIFICATION, DRIVER'S LICENSE STATUS, OPERATOR'S MARITAL STATUS, RESIDENCE ADDRESS, MAILING ADDRESS, RATING TERRITORY, DISCOUNT ELIGIBILITY, PERSON OF LEGAL DRIVING AGE, HOUSEHOLD RESIDENT, and COVERED PERSON. For example, changing the primary garaging address of a covered vehicle may result in a premium adjustment, as it affects risk exposure. Similarly, a change in marital status or household composition may alter discount eligibility and premium calculations. These relationships highlight the ongoing nature of policy management during the policy period. [Data: Entities (334, 335, 336, 337, 338, 339, 340, 341, 352, 353, 354); Relationships (442, 443, 444, 445, 446, 447, 448, 449, 451, 452, 453, +more)]

## The role of INCEPTION in initiating coverage

INCEPTION marks the official start date of the policy, after which coverage becomes active and any changes made by the policyholder are subject to the terms of the policy. This date is critical because it determines when the insurer’s obligations begin and when the policy period officially commences. The relationship between the POLICY PERIOD and INCEPTION is direct and foundational, as the policy period begins precisely at inception. Any events occurring before this date are not covered, even if the application was submitted earlier. This ensures that coverage is only active during the defined window and prevents retroactive claims. [Data: Entities (342); Relationships (450)]

## Geographic and territorial constraints on coverage

The POLICY PERIOD is explicitly tied to a defined TERRITORY, which includes the U.S., Canada, or while being transported between ports. This geographic limitation ensures that coverage applies only within specified regions, and any activity outside these areas may fall outside the scope of protection. The RATING TERRITORY, which is used to determine premium rates, may also change during the policy period, potentially leading to a premium adjustment. These geographic factors are critical in assessing risk and ensuring that coverage aligns with the policyholder’s actual location and travel patterns. [Data: Entities (315, 340); Relationships (396, 448)]

## Reporting obligations triggered by changes during the policy period

The policyholder is required to report changes to key personal and household factors during the policy period, including changes in residence address, mailing address, household residents, or the presence of a person of legal driving age. These changes may affect coverage, premium, or discount eligibility and must be disclosed to maintain policy integrity. Failure to report such changes can result in coverage denial or premium adjustments. The relationships between the POLICY PERIOD and entities like RESIDENCE ADDRESS, HOUSEHOLD RESIDENT, and PERSON OF LEGAL DRIVING AGE emphasize the ongoing nature of policy compliance. [Data: Entities (338, 339, 353, 352); Relationships (446, 447, 451, 452)]

## The impact of driver and household status on policy terms

Changes in driver or household status—such as obtaining a driver’s license, changing marital status, or adding a new household resident—can directly affect the policy’s terms. For instance, a new driver of legal age in the household may increase risk exposure and lead to higher premiums. Similarly, a change in marital status may alter discount eligibility or coverage needs. These dynamic factors are continuously monitored during the policy period, and their impact is governed by the policy’s terms. The relationships between the POLICY PERIOD and DRIVER'S LICENSE STATUS, OPERATOR'S MARITAL STATUS, and HOUSEHOLD RESIDENT reflect the adaptive nature of insurance policies. [Data: Entities (336, 337, 353); Relationships (444, 445, 452)]

## Coverage and protection for covered persons

The COVERED PERSON is an individual protected under the policy, including the named insured and others such as family members or authorized drivers. Their presence and status during the policy period directly influence coverage and premium calculations. Any changes in the identity or status of a covered person must be reported and may result in adjustments to the policy. The relationship between the POLICY PERIOD and COVERED PERSON ensures that protection is active only for those legally recognized as covered during the defined time frame. [Data: Entities (354); Relationships (453)]"

## UNREASONABLE OR UNNECESSARY MEDICAL EXPENSES

If an insured person incurs expenses for medical services that we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary, we may refuse to pay for those expenses and contest them.

## INSURING AGREEMENT

In return for your payment of the premium, we agree to insure you subject to all the terms, conditions and limitations of this policy . We will insure you for the coverages and the limits of liability shown on this policy's declarations page . Your policy consists of the policy contract, your insurance application, the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy .

## GENERAL DEFINITIONS

The following definitions apply throughout the policy . Defined terms are printed in boldface type and have the same meaning whether in the singular, plural, or any other form.

- 1 . ' Additional auto ' means an auto you become the owner of during the policy period that does not permanently replace an auto shown on the declarations page

- b. the additional auto is not covered by any other insurance policy;
- c. you notify us within 30 days of becoming the owner of the additional auto ; and
- d. you pay any additional premium due.

An additional auto will have the broadest coverage we provide for any auto shown on the declarations page .  If you ask us to insure an additional auto more than 30 days after you become the owner, any coverage we provide will begin at the time you request coverage.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COLLISION COVERAGE

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COMPREHENSIVE COVERAGE

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to a:

- 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or
2. non-owned auto ;

and its custom parts or equipment , that is not caused by collision .

## A loss not caused by collision includes:

- 1 . contact with an animal (including a bird);
2. explosion or earthquake;
3. fire;
4. malicious mischief or vandalism;
5. missiles or falling objects;
6. riot or civil commotion;
- 7 . theft or larceny;
8. windstorm, hail, water or flood; or
9. breakage of glass not caused by collision .

## In addition, we will pay for:

- 1 . reasonable transportation expenses incurred by you if a covered auto is stolen; and
2. loss of use damages that you are legally liable to pay if a non-owned auto is stolen. A combined maximum of $900, not exceeding $30 per day, will apply to these additional benefits. The additional benefit for transportation expenses will not apply if you purchased Rental Reimbursement Coverage for the stolen covered auto .

Coverage for transportation expenses and loss of use damages begins 48 hours after you report the theft to us and ends the earliest of:

- 1 . when the auto has been recovered and returned to you or its owner;

We must receive written proof of transportation expenses and loss of use damages.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-RENTAL REIMBURSEMENT COVERAGE

We will reimburse rental charges incurred when you rent an auto from a rental agency or auto repair shop due to a loss to a covered auto for which Rental Reimbursement Coverage has been purchased. Additional fees or charges for insurance, damage waivers, optional equipment, fuel, or accessories are not covered.

This coverage is limited to the each day limit shown on the declarations page for a maximum of 30 days.

## LIMITS OF LIABILITY

The limit of liability shown on the declarations page for  Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage is the most we will pay regardless of the number of:

60|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY refers to the use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation, including activities conducted through transportation network companies (TNCs) such as ride-hailing platforms. This activity is explicitly excluded from coverage under the policy, regardless of whether the vehicle is used for personal or commercial purposes. The exclusion applies from the moment a user logs on to the TNC’s system until they log out, encompassing all time spent en route to pick up passengers, transporting them, or waiting for a ride request. This includes both the actual passenger transport and any associated travel time between pickups and drop-offs.

RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is distinct from the shared-expense carpool exception, which allows limited coverage for non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements among passengers. In contrast, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY involves compensation, meaning the driver receives payment for transporting others, and thus does not qualify for the carpool exception. The policy clearly excludes coverage for any use of a covered auto in connection with commercial ride-sharing services, whether the driver is operating as an independent contractor or under a formal TNC agreement.

The exclusion applies broadly to all forms of compensated passenger transportation, including but not limited to rides provided via smartphone applications, dispatch services, or other digital platforms. This includes scenarios where the vehicle is used to transport persons or property for payment, even if the driver is not formally employed by the TNC. The exclusion remains in effect throughout the entire duration of the ride-sharing activity, from the initial login to the final logout, ensuring that no part of the activity is covered under the policy.

In summary, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is a defined exclusion under the policy, covering any use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation through a transportation network company. It includes all phases of the service—logging in, traveling to pick up passengers, transporting them, and returning to service—regardless of whether the driver is actively matched with a passenger. This exclusion is absolute and does not extend to the shared-expense carpool exception, which only applies to non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements. As such, any vehicle used for compensated ride-sharing is not covered under the policy, and drivers engaging in such activities assume full personal liability for any incidents that may occur.|7

60|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY refers to the use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation, including activities conducted through transportation network companies (TNCs) such as ride-hailing platforms. This activity is explicitly excluded from coverage under the policy, regardless of whether the vehicle is used for personal or commercial purposes. The exclusion applies from the moment a user logs on to the TNC’s system until they log out, encompassing all time spent en route to pick up passengers, transporting them, or waiting for a ride request. This includes both the actual passenger transport and any associated travel time between pickups and drop-offs.

RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is distinct from the shared-expense carpool exception, which allows limited coverage for non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements among passengers. In contrast, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY involves compensation, meaning the driver receives payment for transporting others, and thus does not qualify for the carpool exception. The policy clearly excludes coverage for any use of a covered auto in connection with commercial ride-sharing services, whether the driver is operating as an independent contractor or under a formal TNC agreement.

The exclusion applies broadly to all forms of compensated passenger transportation, including but not limited to rides provided via smartphone applications, dispatch services, or other digital platforms. This includes scenarios where the vehicle is used to transport persons or property for payment, even if the driver is not formally employed by the TNC. The exclusion remains in effect throughout the entire duration of the ride-sharing activity, from the initial login to the final logout, ensuring that no part of the activity is covered under the policy.

In summary, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is a defined exclusion under the policy, covering any use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation through a transportation network company. It includes all phases of the service—logging in, traveling to pick up passengers, transporting them, and returning to service—regardless of whether the driver is actively matched with a passenger. This exclusion is absolute and does not extend to the shared-expense carpool exception, which only applies to non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements. As such, any vehicle used for compensated ride-sharing is not covered under the policy, and drivers engaging in such activities assume full personal liability for any incidents that may occur.|7

60|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY refers to the use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation, including activities conducted through transportation network companies (TNCs) such as ride-hailing platforms. This activity is explicitly excluded from coverage under the policy, regardless of whether the vehicle is used for personal or commercial purposes. The exclusion applies from the moment a user logs on to the TNC’s system until they log out, encompassing all time spent en route to pick up passengers, transporting them, or waiting for a ride request. This includes both the actual passenger transport and any associated travel time between pickups and drop-offs.

RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is distinct from the shared-expense carpool exception, which allows limited coverage for non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements among passengers. In contrast, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY involves compensation, meaning the driver receives payment for transporting others, and thus does not qualify for the carpool exception. The policy clearly excludes coverage for any use of a covered auto in connection with commercial ride-sharing services, whether the driver is operating as an independent contractor or under a formal TNC agreement.

The exclusion applies broadly to all forms of compensated passenger transportation, including but not limited to rides provided via smartphone applications, dispatch services, or other digital platforms. This includes scenarios where the vehicle is used to transport persons or property for payment, even if the driver is not formally employed by the TNC. The exclusion remains in effect throughout the entire duration of the ride-sharing activity, from the initial login to the final logout, ensuring that no part of the activity is covered under the policy.

In summary, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is a defined exclusion under the policy, covering any use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation through a transportation network company. It includes all phases of the service—logging in, traveling to pick up passengers, transporting them, and returning to service—regardless of whether the driver is actively matched with a passenger. This exclusion is absolute and does not extend to the shared-expense carpool exception, which only applies to non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements. As such, any vehicle used for compensated ride-sharing is not covered under the policy, and drivers engaging in such activities assume full personal liability for any incidents that may occur.|7

60|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY refers to the use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation, including activities conducted through transportation network companies (TNCs) such as ride-hailing platforms. This activity is explicitly excluded from coverage under the policy, regardless of whether the vehicle is used for personal or commercial purposes. The exclusion applies from the moment a user logs on to the TNC’s system until they log out, encompassing all time spent en route to pick up passengers, transporting them, or waiting for a ride request. This includes both the actual passenger transport and any associated travel time between pickups and drop-offs.

RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is distinct from the shared-expense carpool exception, which allows limited coverage for non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements among passengers. In contrast, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY involves compensation, meaning the driver receives payment for transporting others, and thus does not qualify for the carpool exception. The policy clearly excludes coverage for any use of a covered auto in connection with commercial ride-sharing services, whether the driver is operating as an independent contractor or under a formal TNC agreement.

The exclusion applies broadly to all forms of compensated passenger transportation, including but not limited to rides provided via smartphone applications, dispatch services, or other digital platforms. This includes scenarios where the vehicle is used to transport persons or property for payment, even if the driver is not formally employed by the TNC. The exclusion remains in effect throughout the entire duration of the ride-sharing activity, from the initial login to the final logout, ensuring that no part of the activity is covered under the policy.

In summary, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is a defined exclusion under the policy, covering any use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation through a transportation network company. It includes all phases of the service—logging in, traveling to pick up passengers, transporting them, and returning to service—regardless of whether the driver is actively matched with a passenger. This exclusion is absolute and does not extend to the shared-expense carpool exception, which only applies to non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements. As such, any vehicle used for compensated ride-sharing is not covered under the policy, and drivers engaging in such activities assume full personal liability for any incidents that may occur.|7

60|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY refers to the use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation, including activities conducted through transportation network companies (TNCs) such as ride-hailing platforms. This activity is explicitly excluded from coverage under the policy, regardless of whether the vehicle is used for personal or commercial purposes. The exclusion applies from the moment a user logs on to the TNC’s system until they log out, encompassing all time spent en route to pick up passengers, transporting them, or waiting for a ride request. This includes both the actual passenger transport and any associated travel time between pickups and drop-offs.

RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is distinct from the shared-expense carpool exception, which allows limited coverage for non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements among passengers. In contrast, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY involves compensation, meaning the driver receives payment for transporting others, and thus does not qualify for the carpool exception. The policy clearly excludes coverage for any use of a covered auto in connection with commercial ride-sharing services, whether the driver is operating as an independent contractor or under a formal TNC agreement.

The exclusion applies broadly to all forms of compensated passenger transportation, including but not limited to rides provided via smartphone applications, dispatch services, or other digital platforms. This includes scenarios where the vehicle is used to transport persons or property for payment, even if the driver is not formally employed by the TNC. The exclusion remains in effect throughout the entire duration of the ride-sharing activity, from the initial login to the final logout, ensuring that no part of the activity is covered under the policy.

In summary, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is a defined exclusion under the policy, covering any use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation through a transportation network company. It includes all phases of the service—logging in, traveling to pick up passengers, transporting them, and returning to service—regardless of whether the driver is actively matched with a passenger. This exclusion is absolute and does not extend to the shared-expense carpool exception, which only applies to non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements. As such, any vehicle used for compensated ride-sharing is not covered under the policy, and drivers engaging in such activities assume full personal liability for any incidents that may occur.|7

The community centers on the Declarations Page, a foundational document within the Maine Auto Policy that consolidates essential policy terms, including coverage details, liability limits, premium amounts, and covered vehicles. ## The Declarations Page as the core policy document

The Declarations Page is the central and most critical document within the insurance policy framework, serving as a legally binding summary of the policy’s key terms. It contains essential information such as the named insured, policy number, policy period, types of coverage, liability limits, and premium amounts. This document ensures transparency and consistency in policy administration, claims processing, and renewal procedures. Its role as a foundational component is reinforced by its inclusion in the broader policy package and its use as a primary reference for both the insured and the insurer. The Underwriting Company is the insurance provider responsible for issuing the policy and is explicitly named on the Declarations Page. It is referred to as 'we,' 'us,' or 'our' within the policy documents, indicating its legal and operational role as the contracting party. This entity bears the financial and legal responsibility for honoring claims under the policy, including those related to uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage. The relationship between the Underwriting Company and the Declarations Page is fundamental, as the page formally identifies the insurer and establishes the basis for the policyholder’s rights and obligations. The Underwriting Company’s credibility and compliance with regulatory standards directly impact the policy’s validity and enforceability [Data: Entities (50), Relationships (54, +more)].

The Auto Insurance Coverage Summary is functionally equivalent to the Declarations Page, serving as an alternative name for the same document. This dual designation indicates that the document is consistently referred to across different contexts and systems within the insurance process. Both terms describe a single, unified document that presents critical policy information such as coverages, limits of liability, covered autos, and premium amounts. The equivalence reinforces the document’s standardized role in policy administration and ensures that stakeholders can identify and access the same information regardless of the terminology used. This consistency supports clarity and reduces the risk of misinterpretation during claims or policy reviews [Data: Entities (48), Relationships (53, +more)].

## Geographic scope of coverage defined by the Declarations Page

The Declarations Page explicitly defines the geographic scope of the policy’s coverage, extending to all U.S. states, U.S. possessions, Canadian provinces, and Canadian territories. This coverage is contingent upon accidents or losses occurring within these jurisdictions, as specified on the Declarations Page. The inclusion of U.S. possessions such as American Samoa and Canadian provinces and territories like the Northwest Territories and Yukon ensures that the policy provides broad protection for policyholders traveling or operating vehicles across North America. This geographic delineation is critical for determining claim eligibility and is directly tied to the Declarations Page, which serves as the authoritative source for coverage boundaries [Data: Entities (355, 331, 332, 333), Relationships (413, 415, 416, 417, +more)].

## Coverage for uninsured/underinsured motorist protection

The Declarations Page specifically outlines the coverage limits for Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage, a critical component of the policy that protects the insured in the event of an accident involving a driver without insurance or with insufficient coverage. This information is essential for determining the insurer’s financial responsibility and the policyholder’s potential recovery. The explicit inclusion of these limits on the Declarations Page ensures that both the insured and the insurer have a clear understanding of the extent of protection provided. This detail is particularly important in claims involving third-party liability and helps prevent disputes over coverage amounts during the claims process [Data: Entities (11), Relationships (413, 415, 416, 417, +more)].

## Role of the Declarations Page in claims and policy administration

The Declarations Page plays a pivotal role in claims processing and policy administration by providing a centralized, authoritative source of policy terms. It enables insurers and policyholders to quickly verify coverage details, liability limits, and premium obligations. During a claim, the Declarations Page is referenced to confirm whether the incident falls within the policy’s scope and to determine the applicable coverage limits. Its use in renewal procedures ensures continuity and consistency in policy terms. The document’s structured format and legal standing make it indispensable for maintaining operational efficiency and regulatory compliance in insurance operations [Data: Entities (11), Relationships (54, 413, 415, 416, 417, +more)].

## Legal and regulatory significance of the Declarations Page

As a legally binding component of the insurance contract, the Declarations Page holds significant weight in legal and regulatory contexts. It serves as evidence of the agreed-upon terms between the insurer and the insured, and its contents can be cited in disputes, audits, or regulatory reviews. The document’s inclusion of policy numbers, named insureds, and coverage limits ensures traceability and accountability. Regulatory bodies may reference the Declarations Page to verify compliance with state and federal insurance laws, particularly regarding minimum coverage requirements and consumer disclosure standards. Its legal status underscores the importance of accuracy and integrity in its preparation and distribution [Data: Entities (11), Relationships (54, 413, 415, 416, 417, +more)]."

60|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY refers to the use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation, including activities conducted through transportation network companies (TNCs) such as ride-hailing platforms. This activity is explicitly excluded from coverage under the policy, regardless of whether the vehicle is used for personal or commercial purposes. The exclusion applies from the moment a user logs on to the TNC’s system until they log out, encompassing all time spent en route to pick up passengers, transporting them, or waiting for a ride request. This includes both the actual passenger transport and any associated travel time between pickups and drop-offs.

RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is distinct from the shared-expense carpool exception, which allows limited coverage for non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements among passengers. In contrast, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY involves compensation, meaning the driver receives payment for transporting others, and thus does not qualify for the carpool exception. The policy clearly excludes coverage for any use of a covered auto in connection with commercial ride-sharing services, whether the driver is operating as an independent contractor or under a formal TNC agreement.

The exclusion applies broadly to all forms of compensated passenger transportation, including but not limited to rides provided via smartphone applications, dispatch services, or other digital platforms. This includes scenarios where the vehicle is used to transport persons or property for payment, even if the driver is not formally employed by the TNC. The exclusion remains in effect throughout the entire duration of the ride-sharing activity, from the initial login to the final logout, ensuring that no part of the activity is covered under the policy.

In summary, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is a defined exclusion under the policy, covering any use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation through a transportation network company. It includes all phases of the service—logging in, traveling to pick up passengers, transporting them, and returning to service—regardless of whether the driver is actively matched with a passenger. This exclusion is absolute and does not extend to the shared-expense carpool exception, which only applies to non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements. 2|INSURER and the Maine Auto Policy Community|"# INSURER and the Maine Auto Policy Community

The community centers on the INSURER, the primary entity responsible for administering the Maine Auto Policy, which governs insurance coverage, claims settlement, and risk management. Key entities include the INSURED, CLAIMANT, MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDER, and various systems such as ESTIMATING SYSTEM and INJURY EVALUATION SYSTEM, all interconnected through processes like claims settlement, premium adjustments, and legal defense. The INSURER maintains control over policy terms, claim evaluations, and recovery efforts, while also managing obligations related to uninsured motorist coverage, loss of earnings, and attorney fees. The community operates under strict legal and procedural frameworks, including requirements for written consent, duty to report changes, and prohibitions against fraud or misrepresentation.

## The INSURER as the central administrative and legal authority

The INSURER is the dominant entity in this community, serving as the central administrative and legal authority for the Maine Auto Policy. It is responsible for underwriting, issuing policies, managing claims, defending insured parties in liability claims, and pursuing recovery from third parties. The INSURER’s role spans the entire insurance lifecycle, from policy inception to claims resolution and recovery, ensuring compliance with both policy language and state law. Its authority is reinforced by its ability to issue endorsements, adjust premiums, and enforce policy conditions, making it the primary guarantor of coverage and accountability. [Data: Entities (24), Relationships (49, 50, 424, 423, 419, 420, 421, 422, 489, 488, +more)]

## Claims settlement as a core operational process

The settlement of claims is a central process in the community, involving multiple systems and entities. The INSURER uses estimating, appraisal, and injury evaluation systems—supported by computer software, databases, and specialized technology—to assess damages, repair costs, and personal injury. These systems are integral to determining the validity and amount of claims, ensuring that payouts align with policy terms and legal standards. The process is formalized through the SETTLEMENT OF CLAIMS entity, which connects directly to the INSURER, claimants, and technical systems. This structured approach enables efficient and consistent claim handling while minimizing disputes. [Data: Entities (326), Relationships (424, 427, 428, 429, 430, 431, 432, 425, +more)]

## Uninsured Motorist Coverage and its conditional application

Uninsured Motorist Coverage provides financial protection to the insured when injured by an uninsured or underinsured driver, but only after all applicable bodily injury liability bonds and policies have been exhausted. This means that the insurer is not obligated to pay until the limits of other liability coverages are fully used through judgments or settlements. The coverage is subject to policy limits and conditions, and the insurer may require written consent before a lawsuit against an uninsured motorist is binding. This creates a layered liability structure where the insurer’s obligation is deferred until other sources of recovery are exhausted. [Data: Entities (132, 142), Relationships (164, 166, 183, +more)]

## Legal and financial obligations related to medical expenses and legal defense

The INSURER is responsible for covering medical expenses deemed reasonable and necessary, but may refuse payment for expenses deemed unreasonable or unnecessary. If a medical service provider sues the insured over unpaid bills, the insurer is obligated to cover defense costs and judgments up to the policy limit. Additionally, the insurer is responsible for a pro rata share of attorney fees incurred by the insured in recovering payments from liable parties. These obligations are balanced by the insurer’s right to recover collection expenses and attorney fees from the deductible reimbursement, which reduces the amount available to the insured. [Data: Entities (129, 126, 378, 379, 380), Relationships (172, 488, 489, +more)]

## The role of the claimant and the risk of fraud or misrepresentation

The CLAIMANT is the individual who files a claim under the policy, and their conduct is subject to scrutiny for fraud or misrepresentation. The policy explicitly prohibits false statements, concealment, or fraudulent behavior by the policyholder or applicant, which can result in denial of coverage or policy cancellation. The INSURER has the right to deny claims or terminate policies if such misconduct is substantiated, particularly if it affects risk assessment or claim validity. This provision reinforces the principle of good faith in insurance contracts and protects the integrity of the system. The claimant’s actions are thus closely monitored, and any material misrepresentation—whether intentional or unintentional—can have serious consequences. [Data: Entities (330, 14), Relationships (425, 41, +more)]

## Transfer of interest and continuity of coverage after death

The policy includes a transfer of interest clause that restricts the transfer of policy rights and duties to another person without written consent, except in the case of the named insured’s death. In such cases, the legal representative of the deceased insured continues to be covered under the policy until the end of the policy period. This ensures continuity of protection and prevents unauthorized transfers, while also maintaining the insurer’s control over policy administration. The legal representative is recognized as a covered party under the policy, allowing for claims to be processed and settlements to be made on behalf of the deceased. [Data: Entities (327, 351), Relationships (433, 435, +more)]

## Premium adjustments and the duty to report changes

The INSURER has the authority to adjust premiums based on updated or incorrect information provided by the policyholder, such as changes in driver status, vehicle use, or household composition. The policyholder has a duty to report changes promptly, and failure to do so may result in premium adjustments or even coverage denial. This requirement ensures that risk assessments remain accurate and that the policy reflects current conditions. The insurer may also issue endorsements to modify policy terms, but only with written consent, reinforcing the formal nature of policy changes. [Data: Entities (27, 323, 322), Relationships (423, 420, 419, +more)]

## Loss of earnings and reimbursement under insurer direction

The policy includes a provision for reimbursement of loss of earnings, up to $200 per day, when the insured is required by the insurer to take time off work for claim-related activities such as attending legal proceedings, providing documentation, or undergoing medical evaluations. This reimbursement is not automatic and is contingent upon the insurer’s request. The policy recognizes the financial burden on the insured during the claims process and aims to prevent penalization for cooperating with the insurer. The daily cap ensures that reimbursements remain within defined limits while still offering meaningful support. [Data: Entities (77), Relationships (87, +more)]

## The insurer’s recovery rights and collection expenses

The INSURER has the authority to pursue recovery from liable third parties or, in certain cases, from insured individuals when payments are made under the policy that may be recoverable. This includes incurring collection expenses such as legal and administrative costs, which can reduce the amount of deductible reimbursement available to the insured. The insurer may also reduce deductible reimbursement based on these expenses, creating a financial incentive to minimize recovery costs. This recovery mechanism helps mitigate financial losses and ensures proper allocation of responsibility, reinforcing the insurer’s role in managing risk and maintaining financial stability. [Data: Entities (380, 378), Relationships (489, 490, +more)]

## The importance of written consent in legal settlements

A judgment or settlement against an uninsured motorist is not binding on the insurer unless it is made with the insurer’s written consent. This requirement ensures that the insurer maintains control over its financial exposure and prevents unauthorized settlements that could exceed policy limits. The written consent clause protects the insurer from unexpected liabilities and ensures that all legal actions are aligned with policy terms. This provision underscores the insurer’s central role in managing legal risks and maintaining compliance with contractual obligations. [Data: Entities (140), Relationships (183, +more)]"

## INSURING AGREEMENT

In return for your payment of the premium, we agree to insure you subject to all the terms, conditions and limitations of this policy . We will insure you for the coverages and the limits of liability shown on this policy's declarations page . Your policy consists of the policy contract, your insurance application, the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy .

## GENERAL DEFINITIONS

The following definitions apply throughout the policy . Defined terms are printed in boldface type and have the same meaning whether in the singular, plural, or any other form.

- 1 . ' Additional auto ' means an auto you become the owner of during the policy period that does not permanently replace an auto shown on the declarations page
- if:
- a. we insure all other autos you own;
- b. the additional auto is not covered by any other insurance policy;
- c. you notify us within 30 days of becoming the owner of the additional auto ; and
- d. you pay any additional premium due.

An additional auto will have the broadest coverage we provide for any auto shown on the declarations page .  If you ask us to insure an additional auto more than 30 days after you become the owner, any coverage we provide will begin at the time you request coverage.

2|URING AGREEMENT

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay damages for bodily injury and property damage for which an insured person becomes legally responsible because of an accident.

Damages include prejudgment interest awarded against an insured person .

We will settle or defend, at our option, any claim for damages covered by this Part I.

## ADDITIONAL DEFINITION

When used in this Part I:

## ' Insured person ' means:

- a. you , a relative , or a rated resident with respect to an accident arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use of an auto or a trailer ;
- b. any person with respect to an accident arising out of that person's use of a covered auto with the permission of you , a relative , or a rated resident ;
- c. any person or organization with respect only to vicarious liability for the acts or omissions of a person described in a. or b. above; and
- d. any ' Additional Interest' shown on the declarations page with respect only to its liability for the acts or omissions of a person described in a. or b. above.

## ADDITIONAL PAYMENTS

In addition to our limit of liability , we will pay for an insured person :

- 1 . all expenses we incur in the settlement of any claim or defense of any lawsuit;
2. interest accruing after entry of judgment, until we have paid, offered to pay , or deposited in court, that portion of the judgment which does not exceed our limit of liability .   This does not apply if we have not been given notice of suit or the opportunity to defend an insured person ;
3. the premium on any appeal bond or attachment bond required in any lawsuit we defend. We have no duty to purchase a bond in an amount exceeding our limit of liability , and we have no duty to apply for or furnish these bonds;
4. up to $250 for a bail bond required because of an accident resulting in bodily injury or property damage covered under this Part I. We have no duty to apply for or furnish this bond; and
5. reasonable expenses, including loss of earnings up to $200 per day, incurred at our request.

## EXCLUSIONS-READ THE FOLLOWING EXCLUSIONS CAREFULLY. IF AN EXCLUSION APPLIES, COVERAGE WILL NOT BE AFFORDED UNDER THIS PART I.

Coverage under this Part I, including our duty to defend, will not apply to any insured person for:

- 1 . bodily injury or property damage arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use of any vehicle or trailer while being used:
- a. to carry persons or property for compensation or a fee;
- b. for retail or wholesale delivery , including, but not limited to, the pickup, transport or delivery of magazines, newspapers, mail or food; or
- c. for ride-sharing activity .

This exclusion does not apply to shared-expense car pools;

2. any liability assumed under any contract or agreement by you , a relative , or a rated resident ;
3. bodily injury to an employee of that insured person arising out of or within the course of employment. This exclusion does not apply to domestic employees if benefits are neither paid nor required to be provided under workers' compensation, disability benefits, or similar laws;
4. bodily injury or property damage arising out of an accident involving any vehicle while being maintained or used by a person while employed or engaged in any auto business .   This exclusion does not apply to you , a relative , a rated resident , or an agent or employee of you , a relative , or a rated resident , when using a covered auto ;
5. bodily injury or property damage resulting from, or sustained during practice or preparation for:
- a. any pre-arranged or organized racing, stunting, speed or demolition contest or activity; or
- b. any driving activity conducted on a permanent or temporary racetrack or racecourse;
6. bodily injury or property damage due to a nuclear reaction or radiation;
8. 7 . bodily injury or property damage for which insurance:
- a. is afforded under a nuclear energy liability insurance contract; or
- b. would be afforded under a nuclear energy liability insurance contract but for its termination upon exhaustion of its limit of liability;
8. any obligation for which the United States Government is liable under the Federal Tort Claims Act;
9. bodily injury or property damage caused by an intentional act of that insured person , or at the direction of that insured person , even if the actual injury or damage is different than that which was intended or expected;
10. property damage to any property owned by, rented to, being transported by , used by, or in the charge of that insured person .   This exclusion does not apply to:

## LIMITS OF LIABILITY

The limit of liability shown on the declarations page for liability coverage is the most we will pay regardless of the number of:

If there is any other applicable liability insurance or bond, any liability insurance we provide will be excess over any other applicable liability insurance or bond.
