A key feature of PART II-MEDICAL PAYMENTS COVERAGE is its reimbursement mechanism in cases where the insured recovers compensation from a third party, such as through a lawsuit or settlement. In such instances, the insurer has a legal right to recover the amounts it paid under this coverage from the third-party recovery. This recovery right ensures that the insurer is not left bearing the full cost when a responsible party is identified and held accountable. The extent of recovery is generally limited to the amount paid by the insurer under Part II, and it is subject to the terms and conditions outlined in the policy.

This coverage is often considered a valuable component of personal auto insurance policies, as it provides a safety net for medical costs that may arise from accidents involving vehicles, pedestrians, or other covered incidents. It is important to note that while the coverage is no-fault in nature, it does not replace or limit the rights of the insured to pursue claims against at-fault parties. Instead, it complements those rights by offering immediate financial support.

Overall, PART II-MEDICAL PAYMENTS COVERAGE serves as a critical tool for ensuring timely medical treatment and financial protection for insured individuals following an accident. ## LIMITS OF LIABILITY

The limit of liability shown on the declarations page for liability coverage is the most we will pay regardless of the number of:

- 1 . claims made;
2. covered autos ;
3. insured persons ;
4. lawsuits brought;
5. vehicles involved in the accident; or
6. premiums paid.

## If your declarations page shows a split limit:

- 1 . the amount shown for 'each person' is the most we will pay for all damages due to bodily injury to one person resulting from any one accident;
2. subject to the 'each person' limit, the amount shown for 'each accident' is the most we will pay for all damages due to bodily injury sustained by two or more persons in any one accident; and
3. the amount shown for 'property damage' is the most we will pay for the total of all property damage resulting from any one accident.

The 'each person' limit of liability applies to the total of all claims made for bodily injury to a person and all claims of others derived from such bodily injury , including, but not

limited to, emotional injury or mental anguish resulting from the bodily injury of another or from witnessing the bodily injury to another, loss of society , loss of companionship, loss of services, loss of consortium, and wrongful death.

If  the declarations  page shows  that  'combined  single  limit'  or  'CSL '  applies,  the amount shown is the most we will pay for the total of all damages resulting from any one accident. However, without changing this limit of liability , we will comply with any law that requires us to provide any separate limits.

No one is entitled to duplicate payments for the same elements of damages.

Any payment to a person under this Part I will be reduced by any payment to that person under Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage.

We will not pay under this Part I any expenses paid or payable under Part II-Medical Payments Coverage.

If multiple auto policies issued by us are in effect for you , we will pay no more than the highest limit of liability for this coverage available under any one policy .

An auto and attached trailer are considered one auto .  Therefore, the limits of liability will not be increased for an accident involving an auto that has an attached trailer .

## FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS

When we certify this policy as proof of financial responsibility , this policy will comply with the law to the extent required. The insured person must reimburse us if we make a payment that we would not have made if this policy was not certified as proof of financial responsibility .

## OTHER INSURANCE

If there is any other applicable liability insurance or bond, any liability insurance we provide will be excess over any other applicable liability insurance or bond. If more than one liability insurance policy or bond applies on an excess basis, we will pay only our share of the damages. Our share is the proportion that our limit of liability bears to the total of all applicable limits.

## OUT-OF-STATE COVERAGE

If an accident to which this Part I applies occurs in any state, territory or possession of the United States of America or any province or territory of Canada, other than the one in which a covered auto is principally garaged, and the state, province, territory or possession has:

- 1 . a financial responsibility or similar law requiring limits of liability for bodily injury or property damage higher than the limits shown on the declarations page , this policy will provide the higher limits; or

2. a compulsory insurance or similar law requiring a non-resident to maintain insurance whenever the non-resident uses an auto in that state, province, territory or possession, this policy will provide the greater of:
- a. the required minimum amounts and types of coverage; or
- b. the limits of liability under this policy .

## LIMITS OF LIABILITY

The limit of liability shown on the declarations page for Medical Payments Coverage is the most we will pay for each insured person injured in any one accident, regardless of the number of:

## CANCELLATION

You may cancel this policy during the policy period by calling or writing us and stating the future date you wish the cancellation to be effective.

We may cancel this policy during the policy period by mailing a notice of cancellation to the named insured shown on the declarations page at the last known address appearing in our records.

If the policy is cancelled for nonpayment of premium, we will mail notice of cancellation to you at least 15 days before cancellation takes effect. In all other cases, we will mail notice of cancellation to you at least 25 days before the cancellation takes effect.

We may cancel this policy for any reason if the notice is received by the named insured within the first 59 days of the initial policy period.

After this policy is in effect for more than 59 days, or if this is a renewal or continuation policy , we may cancel only for one or more of the following reasons:

- 1 . nonpayment of premium;
2. material misrepresentation or fraud by you with respect to any material fact in the procurement, continuation, change or renewal of this policy;
3. material misrepresentation or fraud in the submission of any claim under this policy;
4. loss of driving privileges through suspension, revocation or expiration of an operator's license issued to you , any driver in your household, or any regular operator of a covered auto , other than the first or second suspension under:
- a. Title 29-A M.R.S.A §2471(2);
- b. Title 29-A M.R.S.A §2472(2); or
- c. Title 28-A M.R.S.A §2052;
5. loss of driving privileges by you , a relative , a rated resident , or a principal operator of a covered auto through revocation of an operator's license during the policy period or if this policy is a renewal, during its policy period or the 180 days immediately preceding its effective date; or
6. violation of the terms or conditions of this policy .

A postal service certificate of mailing to the named insured at the insured's last known address appearing in our records will be sufficient proof of notice. If this policy is cancelled, coverage will not be provided as of the effective date and time shown in the notice of cancellation. For purposes of cancellation, this policy is neither severable nor divisible.  Any cancellation will be effective for all coverages for all persons and all vehicles.

Upon cancellation, you may be entitled to a premium refund. However, our making or offering of a refund is not a condition of cancellation.

If this policy is cancelled, any refund due will be computed on a daily pro rata basis. However, we will retain a cancellation fee if this policy is cancelled at your request or if cancellation is for nonpayment of premium. A cancellation fee will be charged only during the initial policy period.

## NONRENEWAL

If neither we nor one of our affiliates offers to renew or continue this policy , we will mail notice of nonrenewal to the named insured shown on the declarations page at the last known address appearing in our records. A postal service certificate of mailing to the named insured at the insured's last known address appearing in our records will be sufficient proof of notice. Notice will be mailed more than 33 days before the end of the policy period.

If we or an affiliate offers to renew or continue this policy and you or your representative does not accept, this policy will automatically terminate at the end of the current policy period. 60|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY refers to the use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation, including activities conducted through transportation network companies (TNCs) such as ride-hailing platforms. The exclusion applies from the moment a user logs on to the TNC’s system until they log out, encompassing all time spent en route to pick up passengers, transporting them, or waiting for a ride request. This includes both the actual passenger transport and any associated travel time between pickups and drop-offs.

RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is distinct from the shared-expense carpool exception, which allows limited coverage for non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements among passengers. In contrast, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY involves compensation, meaning the driver receives payment for transporting others, and thus does not qualify for the carpool exception. The policy clearly excludes coverage for any use of a covered auto in connection with commercial ride-sharing services, whether the driver is operating as an independent contractor or under a formal TNC agreement.

The exclusion applies broadly to all forms of compensated passenger transportation, including but not limited to rides provided via smartphone applications, dispatch services, or other digital platforms. This includes scenarios where the vehicle is used to transport persons or property for payment, even if the driver is not formally employed by the TNC. The exclusion remains in effect throughout the entire duration of the ride-sharing activity, from the initial login to the final logout, ensuring that no part of the activity is covered under the policy.

In summary, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is a defined exclusion under the policy, covering any use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation through a transportation network company. It includes all phases of the service—logging in, traveling to pick up passengers, transporting them, and returning to service—regardless of whether the driver is actively matched with a passenger. This exclusion is absolute and does not extend to the shared-expense carpool exception, which only applies to non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements. ## LIMITS OF LIABILITY

The limit of liability shown on the declarations page for liability coverage is the most we will pay regardless of the number of:

- 1 . claims made;
2. covered autos ;
3. insured persons ;
4. lawsuits brought;
5. vehicles involved in the accident; or
6. premiums paid.

## If your declarations page shows a split limit:

- 1 . the amount shown for 'each person' is the most we will pay for all damages due to bodily injury to one person resulting from any one accident;
2. subject to the 'each person' limit, the amount shown for 'each accident' is the most we will pay for all damages due to bodily injury sustained by two or more persons in any one accident; and
3. the amount shown for 'property damage' is the most we will pay for the total of all property damage resulting from any one accident.

The 'each person' limit of liability applies to the total of all claims made for bodily injury to a person and all claims of others derived from such bodily injury , including, but not

limited to, emotional injury or mental anguish resulting from the bodily injury of another or from witnessing the bodily injury to another, loss of society , loss of companionship, loss of services, loss of consortium, and wrongful death.

If  the declarations  page shows  that  'combined  single  limit'  or  'CSL '  applies,  the amount shown is the most we will pay for the total of all damages resulting from any one accident. However, without changing this limit of liability , we will comply with any law that requires us to provide any separate limits.

No one is entitled to duplicate payments for the same elements of damages.

Any payment to a person under this Part I will be reduced by any payment to that person under Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage.

We will not pay under this Part I any expenses paid or payable under Part II-Medical Payments Coverage.

If multiple auto policies issued by us are in effect for you , we will pay no more than the highest limit of liability for this coverage available under any one policy .

An auto and attached trailer are considered one auto .  Therefore, the limits of liability will not be increased for an accident involving an auto that has an attached trailer .

## FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS

When we certify this policy as proof of financial responsibility , this policy will comply with the law to the extent required. The insured person must reimburse us if we make a payment that we would not have made if this policy was not certified as proof of financial responsibility .

## OTHER INSURANCE

If there is any other applicable liability insurance or bond, any liability insurance we provide will be excess over any other applicable liability insurance or bond. If more than one liability insurance policy or bond applies on an excess basis, we will pay only our share of the damages. Our share is the proportion that our limit of liability bears to the total of all applicable limits.

## OUT-OF-STATE COVERAGE

If an accident to which this Part I applies occurs in any state, territory or possession of the United States of America or any province or territory of Canada, other than the one in which a covered auto is principally garaged, and the state, province, territory or possession has:

- 1 . a financial responsibility or similar law requiring limits of liability for bodily injury or property damage higher than the limits shown on the declarations page , this policy will provide the higher limits; or

2. a compulsory insurance or similar law requiring a non-resident to maintain insurance whenever the non-resident uses an auto in that state, province, territory or possession, this policy will provide the greater of:
- a. the required minimum amounts and types of coverage; or
- b. the limits of liability under this policy .

If an insured person incurs expenses for medical services that we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary, we may refuse to pay for those expenses and contest them.

The policy clearly excludes coverage for any use of a covered auto in connection with commercial ride-sharing services, whether the driver is operating as an independent contractor or under a formal TNC agreement.

The exclusion applies broadly to all forms of compensated passenger transportation, including but not limited to rides provided via smartphone applications, dispatch services, or other digital platforms. This includes scenarios where the vehicle is used to transport persons or property for payment, even if the driver is not formally employed by the TNC. The exclusion remains in effect throughout the entire duration of the ride-sharing activity, from the initial login to the final logout, ensuring that no part of the activity is covered under the policy.

In summary, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is a defined exclusion under the policy, covering any use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation through a transportation network company. It includes all phases of the service—logging in, traveling to pick up passengers, transporting them, and returning to service—regardless of whether the driver is actively matched with a passenger. This exclusion is absolute and does not extend to the shared-expense carpool exception, which only applies to non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements. As such, any vehicle used for compensated ride-sharing is not covered under the policy, and drivers engaging in such activities assume full personal liability for any incidents that may occur.|7

60|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY refers to the use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation, including activities conducted through transportation network companies (TNCs) such as ride-hailing platforms. This activity is explicitly excluded from coverage under the policy, regardless of whether the vehicle is used for personal or commercial purposes. This includes both the actual passenger transport and any associated travel time between pickups and drop-offs.

RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is distinct from the shared-expense carpool exception, which allows limited coverage for non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements among passengers. In contrast, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY involves compensation, meaning the driver receives payment for transporting others, and thus does not qualify for the carpool exception. The policy clearly excludes coverage for any use of a covered auto in connection with commercial ride-sharing services, whether the driver is operating as an independent contractor or under a formal TNC agreement.

The exclusion applies broadly to all forms of compensated passenger transportation, including but not limited to rides provided via smartphone applications, dispatch services, or other digital platforms. This includes scenarios where the vehicle is used to transport persons or property for payment, even if the driver is not formally employed by the TNC. The exclusion remains in effect throughout the entire duration of the ride-sharing activity, from the initial login to the final logout, ensuring that no part of the activity is covered under the policy.

In summary, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is a defined exclusion under the policy, covering any use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation through a transportation network company. It includes all phases of the service—logging in, traveling to pick up passengers, transporting them, and returning to service—regardless of whether the driver is actively matched with a passenger. This exclusion is absolute and does not extend to the shared-expense carpool exception, which only applies to non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements. Instead, it complements those rights by offering immediate financial support.

The bankruptcy or insolvency of an insured person will not relieve us of any obligations under this policy .

## FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS

When we certify this policy as proof of financial responsibility , this policy will comply with the law to the extent required. The insured person must reimburse us if we make a payment that we would not have made if this policy was not certified as proof of financial responsibility .

## OTHER INSURANCE

If there is any other applicable liability insurance or bond, any liability insurance we provide will be excess over any other applicable liability insurance or bond. If more than one liability insurance policy or bond applies on an excess basis, we will pay only our share of the damages. Our share is the proportion that our limit of liability bears to the total of all applicable limits.

## OUT-OF-STATE COVERAGE

- 1 . a financial responsibility or similar law requiring limits of liability for bodily injury or property damage higher than the limits shown on the declarations page , this policy will provide the higher limits; or

2. a compulsory insurance or similar law requiring a non-resident to maintain insurance whenever the non-resident uses an auto in that state, province, territory or possession, this policy will provide the greater of:
- a. the required minimum amounts and types of coverage; or
- b. the limits of liability under this policy .

To prevent overpayment and ensure equitable claims handling, insurers implement a specific rule governing such cases. When multiple auto policies are in effect for the same individual, the insurer will pay no more than the highest limit of liability available under any one of the policies. This rule is designed to avoid duplicate payments and to ensure that the insured receives adequate coverage without exceeding the maximum liability limit provided by a single policy. 112|MULTIPLE AUTO POLICIES|The entity "MULTIPLE AUTO POLICIES" refers to a scenario in which an individual holds more than one auto insurance policy issued by the same insurer. 2|INSURER and the Maine Auto Policy Community|"# INSURER and the Maine Auto Policy Community

The community centers on the INSURER, the primary entity responsible for administering the Maine Auto Policy, which governs insurance coverage, claims settlement, and risk management. Key entities include the INSURED, CLAIMANT, MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDER, and various systems such as ESTIMATING SYSTEM and INJURY EVALUATION SYSTEM, all interconnected through processes like claims settlement, premium adjustments, and legal defense. The INSURER maintains control over policy terms, claim evaluations, and recovery efforts, while also managing obligations related to uninsured motorist coverage, loss of earnings, and attorney fees. The community operates under strict legal and procedural frameworks, including requirements for written consent, duty to report changes, and prohibitions against fraud or misrepresentation.

## The INSURER as the central administrative and legal authority

The INSURER is the dominant entity in this community, serving as the central administrative and legal authority for the Maine Auto Policy. It is responsible for underwriting, issuing policies, managing claims, defending insured parties in liability claims, and pursuing recovery from third parties. The INSURER’s role spans the entire insurance lifecycle, from policy inception to claims resolution and recovery, ensuring compliance with both policy language and state law. Its authority is reinforced by its ability to issue endorsements, adjust premiums, and enforce policy conditions, making it the primary guarantor of coverage and accountability. [Data: Entities (24), Relationships (49, 50, 424, 423, 419, 420, 421, 422, 489, 488, +more)]

## Claims settlement as a core operational process

The settlement of claims is a central process in the community, involving multiple systems and entities. The INSURER uses estimating, appraisal, and injury evaluation systems—supported by computer software, databases, and specialized technology—to assess damages, repair costs, and personal injury. These systems are integral to determining the validity and amount of claims, ensuring that payouts align with policy terms and legal standards. The process is formalized through the SETTLEMENT OF CLAIMS entity, which connects directly to the INSURER, claimants, and technical systems. This structured approach enables efficient and consistent claim handling while minimizing disputes. [Data: Entities (326), Relationships (424, 427, 428, 429, 430, 431, 432, 425, +more)]

## Uninsured Motorist Coverage and its conditional application

Uninsured Motorist Coverage provides financial protection to the insured when injured by an uninsured or underinsured driver, but only after all applicable bodily injury liability bonds and policies have been exhausted. This means that the insurer is not obligated to pay until the limits of other liability coverages are fully used through judgments or settlements. The coverage is subject to policy limits and conditions, and the insurer may require written consent before a lawsuit against an uninsured motorist is binding. This creates a layered liability structure where the insurer’s obligation is deferred until other sources of recovery are exhausted. [Data: Entities (132, 142), Relationships (164, 166, 183, +more)]

## Legal and financial obligations related to medical expenses and legal defense

The INSURER is responsible for covering medical expenses deemed reasonable and necessary, but may refuse payment for expenses deemed unreasonable or unnecessary. If a medical service provider sues the insured over unpaid bills, the insurer is obligated to cover defense costs and judgments up to the policy limit. Additionally, the insurer is responsible for a pro rata share of attorney fees incurred by the insured in recovering payments from liable parties. These obligations are balanced by the insurer’s right to recover collection expenses and attorney fees from the deductible reimbursement, which reduces the amount available to the insured. [Data: Entities (129, 126, 378, 379, 380), Relationships (172, 488, 489, +more)]

## The role of the claimant and the risk of fraud or misrepresentation

The CLAIMANT is the individual who files a claim under the policy, and their conduct is subject to scrutiny for fraud or misrepresentation. The policy explicitly prohibits false statements, concealment, or fraudulent behavior by the policyholder or applicant, which can result in denial of coverage or policy cancellation. The INSURER has the right to deny claims or terminate policies if such misconduct is substantiated, particularly if it affects risk assessment or claim validity. This provision reinforces the principle of good faith in insurance contracts and protects the integrity of the system. The claimant’s actions are thus closely monitored, and any material misrepresentation—whether intentional or unintentional—can have serious consequences. [Data: Entities (330, 14), Relationships (425, 41, +more)]

## Transfer of interest and continuity of coverage after death

The policy includes a transfer of interest clause that restricts the transfer of policy rights and duties to another person without written consent, except in the case of the named insured’s death. In such cases, the legal representative of the deceased insured continues to be covered under the policy until the end of the policy period. This ensures continuity of protection and prevents unauthorized transfers, while also maintaining the insurer’s control over policy administration. The legal representative is recognized as a covered party under the policy, allowing for claims to be processed and settlements to be made on behalf of the deceased. [Data: Entities (327, 351), Relationships (433, 435, +more)]

## Premium adjustments and the duty to report changes

The INSURER has the authority to adjust premiums based on updated or incorrect information provided by the policyholder, such as changes in driver status, vehicle use, or household composition. The policyholder has a duty to report changes promptly, and failure to do so may result in premium adjustments or even coverage denial. This requirement ensures that risk assessments remain accurate and that the policy reflects current conditions. The insurer may also issue endorsements to modify policy terms, but only with written consent, reinforcing the formal nature of policy changes. [Data: Entities (27, 323, 322), Relationships (423, 420, 419, +more)]

## Loss of earnings and reimbursement under insurer direction

The policy includes a provision for reimbursement of loss of earnings, up to $200 per day, when the insured is required by the insurer to take time off work for claim-related activities such as attending legal proceedings, providing documentation, or undergoing medical evaluations. This reimbursement is not automatic and is contingent upon the insurer’s request. The policy recognizes the financial burden on the insured during the claims process and aims to prevent penalization for cooperating with the insurer. The daily cap ensures that reimbursements remain within defined limits while still offering meaningful support. [Data: Entities (77), Relationships (87, +more)]

## The insurer’s recovery rights and collection expenses

The INSURER has the authority to pursue recovery from liable third parties or, in certain cases, from insured individuals when payments are made under the policy that may be recoverable. This includes incurring collection expenses such as legal and administrative costs, which can reduce the amount of deductible reimbursement available to the insured. The insurer may also reduce deductible reimbursement based on these expenses, creating a financial incentive to minimize recovery costs. This recovery mechanism helps mitigate financial losses and ensures proper allocation of responsibility, reinforcing the insurer’s role in managing risk and maintaining financial stability. [Data: Entities (380, 378), Relationships (489, 490, +more)]

## The importance of written consent in legal settlements

A judgment or settlement against an uninsured motorist is not binding on the insurer unless it is made with the insurer’s written consent. This requirement ensures that the insurer maintains control over its financial exposure and prevents unauthorized settlements that could exceed policy limits. The written consent clause protects the insurer from unexpected liabilities and ensures that all legal actions are aligned with policy terms. This provision underscores the insurer’s central role in managing legal risks and maintaining compliance with contractual obligations. [Data: Entities (140), Relationships (183, +more)]"

130|LIMIT OF LIABILITY|The "LIMIT OF LIABILITY" refers to the maximum amount an insurer will pay under a policy for covered losses, which is determined by two distinct but related factors depending on the context of the claim. In the case of medical expenses, the limit represents the maximum amount the insurer will pay per insured person per accident, as specified on the declarations page of the policy. This amount may be subject to reduction by other applicable coverages, such as primary health insurance or other auto insurance policies, which could lower the insurer’s financial responsibility. This medical expense limit is designed to cap the insurer’s exposure while ensuring that covered individuals receive necessary care up to the policy’s stated threshold.

In the context of property damage, particularly for covered autos, the limit of liability is expressed as a percentage of the actual cash value (ACV) of the vehicle at the time of loss. This means that the insurer will not pay more than a specified percentage of the car’s ACV—typically ranging from 80% to 100%, depending on the policy terms—regardless of the cost to repair or replace the vehicle. This cap ensures that the insurer’s liability is limited to a predetermined proportion of the vehicle’s market value, which accounts for depreciation and wear and tear. As a result, if a vehicle is totaled, the insured may receive less than the full cost of a replacement, especially if the ACV is significantly lower than the original purchase price.

Together, these two components define the financial boundaries of the insurer’s obligation under the policy. While the medical expense limit applies to personal injury and healthcare costs, the ACV-based percentage limit applies to physical damage to vehicles. Both are clearly outlined on the declarations page, which serves as the official summary of coverage terms. It is important to note that these limits are not interchangeable and apply to different types of claims. The insurer’s total liability cannot exceed either the per-person medical limit or the percentage-of-ACV cap, whichever is applicable. ## MAINE AUTO POLICY

## INSURING AGREEMENT

In return for your payment of the premium, we agree to insure you subject to all the terms, conditions and limitations of this policy . We will insure you for the coverages and the limits of liability shown on this policy's declarations page . Your policy consists of the policy contract, your insurance application, the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy .

## GENERAL DEFINITIONS

The following definitions apply throughout the policy . Defined terms are printed in boldface type and have the same meaning whether in the singular, plural, or any other form.

- 1 . ' Additional auto ' means an auto you become the owner of during the policy period that does not permanently replace an auto shown on the declarations page
- if:
- a. we insure all other autos you own;
- b. the additional auto is not covered by any other insurance policy;
- c. you notify us within 30 days of becoming the owner of the additional auto ; and
- d. you pay any additional premium due.

An additional auto will have the broadest coverage we provide for any auto shown on the declarations page .  If you ask us to insure an additional auto more than 30 days after you become the owner, any coverage we provide will begin at the time you request coverage.

- 1 . the insured person will be required to sign a document agreeing to reimburse us out of payments made to that insured person from a liable party; and
2. we are responsible for a pro rata share of the attorney fees incurred by that insured person in recovering payment from a liable party.

If an insured person recovers from another without our written consent, and such recovery prejudices our right to recover payment, the insured person's right to payment under any affected coverage will no longer exist.

If we elect to exercise our rights of recovery against another, we will also attempt to recover any deductible incurred by an insured person under this policy unless we are specifically instructed by that person not to pursue the deductible. We have no obligation to pursue recovery against another for any loss not covered by this policy .

We reserve  the  right  to  compromise  or  settle  the  deductible  and  property  damage claims against the responsible parties for less than the full amount. We also reserve the right to incur reasonable expenses and attorney fees in pursuit of the recovery .

If the total recovery is less than the total of our payment and the deductible, we will reduce reimbursement of the deductible based on the proportion that the actual recovery bears to the total of our payment and the deductible. A proportionate share of collection expenses and attorney fees incurred in connection with these recovery efforts will also reduce reimbursement of the deductible.

These provisions will be applied in accordance with state law.

## JOINT AND INDIVIDUAL INTERESTS

If there is more than one named insured on this policy , any named insured may cancel or change this policy. The action of one named insured will be binding on all persons provided coverage under this policy.

## BANKRUPTCY

The bankruptcy or insolvency of an insured person will not relieve us of any obligations under this policy .

## LIMITS OF LIABILITY

The limit of liability shown on the declarations page for liability coverage is the most we will pay regardless of the number of:

- 1 . claims made;
2. covered autos ;
3. insured persons ;
4. lawsuits brought;
5. vehicles involved in the accident; or
6. premiums paid.

## If your declarations page shows a split limit:

- 1 . the amount shown for 'each person' is the most we will pay for all damages due to bodily injury to one person resulting from any one accident;
2. subject to the 'each person' limit, the amount shown for 'each accident' is the most we will pay for all damages due to bodily injury sustained by two or more persons in any one accident; and
3. the amount shown for 'property damage' is the most we will pay for the total of all property damage resulting from any one accident.

The 'each person' limit of liability applies to the total of all claims made for bodily injury to a person and all claims of others derived from such bodily injury , including, but not

limited to, emotional injury or mental anguish resulting from the bodily injury of another or from witnessing the bodily injury to another, loss of society , loss of companionship, loss of services, loss of consortium, and wrongful death.

If  the declarations  page shows  that  'combined  single  limit'  or  'CSL '  applies,  the amount shown is the most we will pay for the total of all damages resulting from any one accident. However, without changing this limit of liability , we will comply with any law that requires us to provide any separate limits.

No one is entitled to duplicate payments for the same elements of damages.

Any payment to a person under this Part I will be reduced by any payment to that person under Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage.

We will not pay under this Part I any expenses paid or payable under Part II-Medical Payments Coverage.

If multiple auto policies issued by us are in effect for you , we will pay no more than the highest limit of liability for this coverage available under any one policy .

An auto and attached trailer are considered one auto .  Therefore, the limits of liability will not be increased for an accident involving an auto that has an attached trailer .

## FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS

When we certify this policy as proof of financial responsibility , this policy will comply with the law to the extent required. The insured person must reimburse us if we make a payment that we would not have made if this policy was not certified as proof of financial responsibility .

## OTHER INSURANCE

If there is any other applicable liability insurance or bond, any liability insurance we provide will be excess over any other applicable liability insurance or bond. If more than one liability insurance policy or bond applies on an excess basis, we will pay only our share of the damages. Our share is the proportion that our limit of liability bears to the total of all applicable limits.

## OUT-OF-STATE COVERAGE

If an accident to which this Part I applies occurs in any state, territory or possession of the United States of America or any province or territory of Canada, other than the one in which a covered auto is principally garaged, and the state, province, territory or possession has:

- 1 . a financial responsibility or similar law requiring limits of liability for bodily injury or property damage higher than the limits shown on the declarations page , this policy will provide the higher limits; or

2. a compulsory insurance or similar law requiring a non-resident to maintain insurance whenever the non-resident uses an auto in that state, province, territory or possession, this policy will provide the greater of:
- a. the required minimum amounts and types of coverage; or
- b. the limits of liability under this policy .

2. whether the medical services are necessary.

In the context of property damage, particularly for covered autos, the limit of liability is expressed as a percentage of the actual cash value (ACV) of the vehicle at the time of loss. This means that the insurer will not pay more than a specified percentage of the car’s ACV—typically ranging from 80% to 100%, depending on the policy terms—regardless of the cost to repair or replace the vehicle. This cap ensures that the insurer’s liability is limited to a predetermined proportion of the vehicle’s market value, which accounts for depreciation and wear and tear. As a result, if a vehicle is totaled, the insured may receive less than the full cost of a replacement, especially if the ACV is significantly lower than the original purchase price.

Together, these two components define the financial boundaries of the insurer’s obligation under the policy. While the medical expense limit applies to personal injury and healthcare costs, the ACV-based percentage limit applies to physical damage to vehicles. Both are clearly outlined on the declarations page, which serves as the official summary of coverage terms. It is important to note that these limits are not interchangeable and apply to different types of claims. The insurer’s total liability cannot exceed either the per-person medical limit or the percentage-of-ACV cap, whichever is applicable. This policy contract, your insurance application (which is made a part of this policy as if attached hereto), the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy issued by us , contain all the agreements between you and us . ## UNREASONABLE OR UNNECESSARY MEDICAL EXPENSES

If an insured person incurs expenses for medical services that we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary, we may refuse to pay for those expenses and contest them.

If the medical service provider sues the insured person because we refuse to pay expenses for medical services that we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary, we will pay any resulting defense costs, and any resulting judgment against the insured person , subject to the limit of liability for this coverage. The insured person may not sue us for expenses for medical services we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary unless the insured person paid the entire disputed amount to the medical service provider or the medical service provider has initiated collection activity against the insured person for the unreasonable or unnecessary expenses.

The coverage level is aligned with the broadest coverage available for other vehicles on the policy, and comprehensive and collision protection are available only if the appropriate premiums are paid. 60|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY refers to the use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation, including activities conducted through transportation network companies (TNCs) such as ride-hailing platforms. This activity is explicitly excluded from coverage under the policy, regardless of whether the vehicle is used for personal or commercial purposes. The exclusion applies from the moment a user logs on to the TNC’s system until they log out, encompassing all time spent en route to pick up passengers, transporting them, or waiting for a ride request. This includes both the actual passenger transport and any associated travel time between pickups and drop-offs.

RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is distinct from the shared-expense carpool exception, which allows limited coverage for non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements among passengers. In contrast, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY involves compensation, meaning the driver receives payment for transporting others, and thus does not qualify for the carpool exception. The policy clearly excludes coverage for any use of a covered auto in connection with commercial ride-sharing services, whether the driver is operating as an independent contractor or under a formal TNC agreement.

The exclusion applies broadly to all forms of compensated passenger transportation, including but not limited to rides provided via smartphone applications, dispatch services, or other digital platforms. This includes scenarios where the vehicle is used to transport persons or property for payment, even if the driver is not formally employed by the TNC. The exclusion remains in effect throughout the entire duration of the ride-sharing activity, from the initial login to the final logout, ensuring that no part of the activity is covered under the policy.

In summary, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is a defined exclusion under the policy, covering any use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation through a transportation network company. It includes all phases of the service—logging in, traveling to pick up passengers, transporting them, and returning to service—regardless of whether the driver is actively matched with a passenger. This exclusion is absolute and does not extend to the shared-expense carpool exception, which only applies to non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements. As such, any vehicle used for compensated ride-sharing is not covered under the policy, and drivers engaging in such activities assume full personal liability for any incidents that may occur.|7

60|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY refers to the use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation, including activities conducted through transportation network companies (TNCs) such as ride-hailing platforms. This activity is explicitly excluded from coverage under the policy, regardless of whether the vehicle is used for personal or commercial purposes. The exclusion applies from the moment a user logs on to the TNC’s system until they log out, encompassing all time spent en route to pick up passengers, transporting them, or waiting for a ride request. This includes both the actual passenger transport and any associated travel time between pickups and drop-offs.

RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is distinct from the shared-expense carpool exception, which allows limited coverage for non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements among passengers. In contrast, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY involves compensation, meaning the driver receives payment for transporting others, and thus does not qualify for the carpool exception. The policy clearly excludes coverage for any use of a covered auto in connection with commercial ride-sharing services, whether the driver is operating as an independent contractor or under a formal TNC agreement.

The exclusion applies broadly to all forms of compensated passenger transportation, including but not limited to rides provided via smartphone applications, dispatch services, or other digital platforms. This includes scenarios where the vehicle is used to transport persons or property for payment, even if the driver is not formally employed by the TNC. The exclusion remains in effect throughout the entire duration of the ride-sharing activity, from the initial login to the final logout, ensuring that no part of the activity is covered under the policy.

In summary, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is a defined exclusion under the policy, covering any use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation through a transportation network company. It includes all phases of the service—logging in, traveling to pick up passengers, transporting them, and returning to service—regardless of whether the driver is actively matched with a passenger. This exclusion is absolute and does not extend to the shared-expense carpool exception, which only applies to non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements. 60|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY|RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY refers to the use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation, including activities conducted through transportation network companies (TNCs) such as ride-hailing platforms. This includes both the actual passenger transport and any associated travel time between pickups and drop-offs.

RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is distinct from the shared-expense carpool exception, which allows limited coverage for non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements among passengers. In contrast, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY involves compensation, meaning the driver receives payment for transporting others, and thus does not qualify for the carpool exception. The policy clearly excludes coverage for any use of a covered auto in connection with commercial ride-sharing services, whether the driver is operating as an independent contractor or under a formal TNC agreement.

The exclusion applies broadly to all forms of compensated passenger transportation, including but not limited to rides provided via smartphone applications, dispatch services, or other digital platforms. This includes scenarios where the vehicle is used to transport persons or property for payment, even if the driver is not formally employed by the TNC. The exclusion remains in effect throughout the entire duration of the ride-sharing activity, from the initial login to the final logout, ensuring that no part of the activity is covered under the policy.

In summary, RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY is a defined exclusion under the policy, covering any use of a vehicle to transport passengers for compensation through a transportation network company. It includes all phases of the service—logging in, traveling to pick up passengers, transporting them, and returning to service—regardless of whether the driver is actively matched with a passenger. This exclusion is absolute and does not extend to the shared-expense carpool exception, which only applies to non-commercial, cost-sharing arrangements. This medical expense limit is designed to cap the insurer’s exposure while ensuring that covered individuals receive necessary care up to the policy’s stated threshold.

In the context of property damage, particularly for covered autos, the limit of liability is expressed as a percentage of the actual cash value (ACV) of the vehicle at the time of loss. This means that the insurer will not pay more than a specified percentage of the car’s ACV—typically ranging from 80% to 100%, depending on the policy terms—regardless of the cost to repair or replace the vehicle. This cap ensures that the insurer’s liability is limited to a predetermined proportion of the vehicle’s market value, which accounts for depreciation and wear and tear. As a result, if a vehicle is totaled, the insured may receive less than the full cost of a replacement, especially if the ACV is significantly lower than the original purchase price.

Together, these two components define the financial boundaries of the insurer’s obligation under the policy. While the medical expense limit applies to personal injury and healthcare costs, the ACV-based percentage limit applies to physical damage to vehicles. Both are clearly outlined on the declarations page, which serves as the official summary of coverage terms. It is important to note that these limits are not interchangeable and apply to different types of claims. The insurer’s total liability cannot exceed either the per-person medical limit or the percentage-of-ACV cap, whichever is applicable. In the context of property damage, particularly for covered autos, the limit of liability is expressed as a percentage of the actual cash value (ACV) of the vehicle at the time of loss. This cap ensures that the insurer’s liability is limited to a predetermined proportion of the vehicle’s market value, which accounts for depreciation and wear and tear. In return for your payment of the premium, we agree to insure you subject to all the terms, conditions and limitations of this policy . We will insure you for the coverages and the limits of liability shown on this policy's declarations page . Your policy consists of the policy contract, your insurance application, the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy .

This cap ensures that the insurer’s liability is limited to a predetermined proportion of the vehicle’s market value, which accounts for depreciation and wear and tear. 148|ARBITRATION|ARBITRATION is a formal, binding dispute resolution process established within the policy framework to address disagreements between the insurer and the insured, particularly in cases involving uninsured motor vehicle accidents. This process is specifically designed to resolve disputes concerning liability or the amount of damages owed when a claim arises from an accident involving an uninsured driver. When such disputes occur, the parties involved may opt for arbitration instead of litigation, allowing for a more streamlined and efficient resolution. The process is governed by predefined rules that outline the selection of impartial arbitrators, who are typically chosen from a designated panel or through mutual agreement between the insurer and the insured. These arbitrators are expected to be neutral and qualified to assess the facts and legal issues at hand. The costs associated with arbitration are generally shared between the parties, though the policy may specify particular cost allocations. Once the arbitrators render a decision, it is binding on both the insurer and the insured, meaning that neither party can appeal the outcome in court, except in rare cases of procedural misconduct or fraud. The arbitration process is intended to provide a fair, timely, and cost-effective alternative to traditional legal proceedings, ensuring that claims are resolved without prolonged delays. By incorporating arbitration into the policy, the insurer aims to promote consistency, reduce legal expenses, and maintain a predictable claims resolution timeline. Overall, ARBITRATION serves as a critical mechanism for resolving contentious issues in uninsured motor vehicle claims, balancing the interests of both the insured and the insurer through a structured, legally enforceable process.|10

## MAINE AUTO POLICY

## INSURING AGREEMENT

In return for your payment of the premium, we agree to insure you subject to all the terms, conditions and limitations of this policy . We will insure you for the coverages and the limits of liability shown on this policy's declarations page . Your policy consists of the policy contract, your insurance application, the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy .

## GENERAL DEFINITIONS

The following definitions apply throughout the policy . Defined terms are printed in boldface type and have the same meaning whether in the singular, plural, or any other form.

- 1 . ' Additional auto ' means an auto you become the owner of during the policy period that does not permanently replace an auto shown on the declarations page
- if:
- a. we insure all other autos you own;
- b. the additional auto is not covered by any other insurance policy;
- c. you notify us within 30 days of becoming the owner of the additional auto ; and
- d. you pay any additional premium due.

An additional auto will have the broadest coverage we provide for any auto shown on the declarations page .  If you ask us to insure an additional auto more than 30 days after you become the owner, any coverage we provide will begin at the time you request coverage.

## UNREASONABLE OR UNNECESSARY MEDICAL EXPENSES

If an insured person incurs expenses for medical services that we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary, we may refuse to pay for those expenses and contest them.

If the medical service provider sues the insured person because we refuse to pay expenses for medical services that we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary, we will pay any resulting defense costs, and any resulting judgment against the insured person , subject to the limit of liability for this coverage. We will choose the counsel. We will also pay reasonable expenses, including loss of earnings up to $200 per day, incurred at our request.

The insured person may not sue us for expenses for medical services we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary unless the insured person paid the entire disputed amount to the medical service provider or the medical service provider has initiated collection activity against the insured person for the unreasonable or unnecessary expenses.

## OTHER INSURANCE

If there is other applicable auto medical payments insurance, we will pay only our share of the loss. Our share is the proportion that our limit of liability bears to the total of all applicable limits. However, any insurance we provide for an insured person occupying a vehicle or trailer, other than a covered auto , will be excess over any other auto insurance providing payments for medical services .

## PART III-UNINSURED/UNDERINSURED MOTORIST COVERAGE

## INSURING AGREEMENT

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for damages that an insured person is legally entitled to recover from the owner or operator of an uninsured motor vehicle because of bodily injury :

- 1 . sustained by an insured person ;
2. caused by an accident; and
3. arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use of an uninsured motor vehicle .

We will pay under this Part III only after the limits of liability under all applicable bodily injury liability bonds and policies have been exhausted by payment of judgments or settlements.

Any judgment or settlement for damages against an owner or operator of an uninsured motor vehicle that arises out of a lawsuit brought without our written consent is not binding on us .

## ADDITIONAL DEFINITIONS

When used in this Part III:

- 1 . ' Insured person ' means:
- a. you , a relative , or a rated resident ;
- b. any person while operating a covered auto with the permission of you , a relative , or a rated resident ;
- c. any person occupying , but not operating, a covered auto ; and
- d. any person who is entitled to recover damages covered by this Part III because of bodily injury sustained by a person described in a., b. or c. above.
2. ' Uninsured motor vehicle ' means a land motor vehicle or trailer of any type:
- a. to which no bodily injury liability bond or policy applies at the time of the accident;
- b. to which a bodily injury liability bond or policy applies at the time of the accident, but the bonding or insuring company:
- (i) denies coverage; or
- (ii) is or becomes insolvent;
- c. to which a bodily injury liability bond or policy applies at the time of the accident, but its limit of liability for bodily injury is less than the minimum limit of liability for bodily injury specified by the financial responsibility law of the state in which the covered auto is principally garaged;
- d. whose owner or operator cannot be identified and which causes an accident resulting in bodily injury to an insured person , provided that the insured person , or someone on his or her behalf, reports the accident to the police or civil authority within 24 hours or as soon as practicable after the accident; or

- e. to which a bodily injury liability bond or policy applies at the time of the accident, but the sum of all applicable limits of liability for bodily injury is less than the  combined sum of the applicable coverage limit for Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage shown on the declarations page and the coverage limits available under all other applicable uninsured or underinsured motorist coverages.

## An ' uninsured motor vehicle ' does not include any vehicle or equipment:

- a. owned by you , a relative , or a rated resident or furnished or available for the regular use of you , a relative , or a rated resident ;
- b. owned or operated by a self-insurer under any applicable motor vehicle law, except a self-insurer that is or becomes insolvent;
- c. operated on rails or crawler treads;
- d. designed mainly for use off public roads, while not on public roads;
- e. while located for use as a residence or premises; or
- f. that is a covered auto .

This amount may be subject to reduction by other applicable coverages, such as primary health insurance or other auto insurance policies, which could lower the insurer’s financial responsibility. This medical expense limit is designed to cap the insurer’s exposure while ensuring that covered individuals receive necessary care up to the policy’s stated threshold.

In the context of property damage, particularly for covered autos, the limit of liability is expressed as a percentage of the actual cash value (ACV) of the vehicle at the time of loss. This means that the insurer will not pay more than a specified percentage of the car’s ACV—typically ranging from 80% to 100%, depending on the policy terms—regardless of the cost to repair or replace the vehicle. This cap ensures that the insurer’s liability is limited to a predetermined proportion of the vehicle’s market value, which accounts for depreciation and wear and tear. As a result, if a vehicle is totaled, the insured may receive less than the full cost of a replacement, especially if the ACV is significantly lower than the original purchase price.

Together, these two components define the financial boundaries of the insurer’s obligation under the policy. While the medical expense limit applies to personal injury and healthcare costs, the ACV-based percentage limit applies to physical damage to vehicles. Both are clearly outlined on the declarations page, which serves as the official summary of coverage terms. It is important to note that these limits are not interchangeable and apply to different types of claims. The insurer’s total liability cannot exceed either the per-person medical limit or the percentage-of-ACV cap, whichever is applicable. The extent of recovery is generally limited to the amount paid by the insurer under Part II, and it is subject to the terms and conditions outlined in the policy.

It is important to note that while the coverage is no-fault in nature, it does not replace or limit the rights of the insured to pursue claims against at-fault parties. Instead, it complements those rights by offering immediate financial support.

Overall, PART II-MEDICAL PAYMENTS COVERAGE serves as a critical tool for ensuring timely medical treatment and financial protection for insured individuals following an accident. 112|MULTIPLE AUTO POLICIES|The entity "MULTIPLE AUTO POLICIES" refers to a scenario in which an individual holds more than one auto insurance policy issued by the same insurer. This situation typically arises when a person owns multiple vehicles or has overlapping coverage periods, resulting in more than one active policy for the same insured party. To prevent overpayment and ensure equitable claims handling, insurers implement a specific rule governing such cases. When multiple auto policies are in effect for the same individual, the insurer will pay no more than the highest limit of liability available under any one of the policies. This rule is designed to avoid duplicate payments and to ensure that the insured receives adequate coverage without exceeding the maximum liability limit provided by a single policy. The application of the highest available limit serves as a safeguard against financial overreach by the insurer while maintaining fairness in claims settlement. This principle applies uniformly regardless of the number of policies in force, as long as they are issued by the same insurer and cover the same individual. The policyholder is not entitled to aggregate the liability limits from multiple policies; instead, the claim will be settled up to the maximum limit offered by the single policy with the highest coverage. This standard practice helps maintain consistency in underwriting, claims processing, and risk management across the insurer’s portfolio. 141|EXCESS INSURANCE|Excess insurance is a type of insurance that provides coverage only after the limits of primary insurance have been exhausted. In such cases, the excess policy will respond to claims only after the primary auto insurance has paid up to its maximum limit. This ensures that the insured maintains protection even for vehicles or liabilities not explicitly included in the primary policy. Excess insurance is particularly valuable in situations involving significant liability exposure, such as in commercial operations, high-value assets, or personal liability scenarios where standard coverage limits may be insufficient. It is important to note that excess insurance does not provide coverage for losses that fall below the primary policy’s deductible or limit; it only applies once the primary coverage has been fully utilized. 130|LIMIT OF LIABILITY|The "LIMIT OF LIABILITY" refers to the maximum amount an insurer will pay under a policy for covered losses, which is determined by two distinct but related factors depending on the context of the claim. In the case of medical expenses, the limit represents the maximum amount the insurer will pay per insured person per accident, as specified on the declarations page of the policy. This amount may be subject to reduction by other applicable coverages, such as primary health insurance or other auto insurance policies, which could lower the insurer’s financial responsibility. This medical expense limit is designed to cap the insurer’s exposure while ensuring that covered individuals receive necessary care up to the policy’s stated threshold.

In the context of property damage, particularly for covered autos, the limit of liability is expressed as a percentage of the actual cash value (ACV) of the vehicle at the time of loss. This means that the insurer will not pay more than a specified percentage of the car’s ACV—typically ranging from 80% to 100%, depending on the policy terms—regardless of the cost to repair or replace the vehicle. This cap ensures that the insurer’s liability is limited to a predetermined proportion of the vehicle’s market value, which accounts for depreciation and wear and tear. As a result, if a vehicle is totaled, the insured may receive less than the full cost of a replacement, especially if the ACV is significantly lower than the original purchase price.

Together, these two components define the financial boundaries of the insurer’s obligation under the policy. While the medical expense limit applies to personal injury and healthcare costs, the ACV-based percentage limit applies to physical damage to vehicles. It is important to note that these limits are not interchangeable and apply to different types of claims. In return for your payment of the premium, we agree to insure you subject to all the terms, conditions and limitations of this policy . Your policy consists of the policy contract, your insurance application, the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy .

148|ARBITRATION|ARBITRATION is a formal, binding dispute resolution process established within the policy framework to address disagreements between the insurer and the insured, particularly in cases involving uninsured motor vehicle accidents. This process is specifically designed to resolve disputes concerning liability or the amount of damages owed when a claim arises from an accident involving an uninsured driver. When such disputes occur, the parties involved may opt for arbitration instead of litigation, allowing for a more streamlined and efficient resolution. The process is governed by predefined rules that outline the selection of impartial arbitrators, who are typically chosen from a designated panel or through mutual agreement between the insurer and the insured. These arbitrators are expected to be neutral and qualified to assess the facts and legal issues at hand. The costs associated with arbitration are generally shared between the parties, though the policy may specify particular cost allocations. Once the arbitrators render a decision, it is binding on both the insurer and the insured, meaning that neither party can appeal the outcome in court, except in rare cases of procedural misconduct or fraud. The arbitration process is intended to provide a fair, timely, and cost-effective alternative to traditional legal proceedings, ensuring that claims are resolved without prolonged delays. By incorporating arbitration into the policy, the insurer aims to promote consistency, reduce legal expenses, and maintain a predictable claims resolution timeline. ## PART IV-DAMAGE TO A VEHICLE

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COLLISION COVERAGE

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to a:

- 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or
2. non-owned auto ;

and its custom parts or equipment , resulting from collision .

In addition, we will pay the reasonable cost to replace any child safety seat damaged in an accident to which this coverage applies.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COMPREHENSIVE COVERAGE

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to a:

- 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or
2. non-owned auto ;

and its custom parts or equipment , that is not caused by collision .

## A loss not caused by collision includes:

- 1 . contact with an animal (including a bird);
2. explosion or earthquake;
3. fire;
4. malicious mischief or vandalism;
5. missiles or falling objects;
6. riot or civil commotion;
- 7 . theft or larceny;
8. windstorm, hail, water or flood; or
9. breakage of glass not caused by collision .

## In addition, we will pay for:

- 1 . reasonable transportation expenses incurred by you if a covered auto is stolen; and
2. loss of use damages that you are legally liable to pay if a non-owned auto is stolen. A combined maximum of $900, not exceeding $30 per day, will apply to these additional benefits. The additional benefit for transportation expenses will not apply if you purchased Rental Reimbursement Coverage for the stolen covered auto .

Coverage for transportation expenses and loss of use damages begins 48 hours after you report the theft to us and ends the earliest of:

- 1 . when the auto has been recovered and returned to you or its owner;
2. when the auto has been recovered and repaired;
3. when the auto has been replaced;
4. 72 hours after we make an offer to settle the loss if the auto is deemed by us to be a total loss; or

5. if the loss is theft of a rented non-owned auto , 30 days after loss of use begins on the loss.

We must receive written proof of transportation expenses and loss of use damages.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-ADDITIONAL CUSTOM PARTS OR EQUIPMENT COVERAGE

We will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to custom parts or equipment on a covered auto for which this coverage has been purchased. This coverage applies only if you have purchased both Comprehensive Coverage and Collision Coverage for that covered auto and the loss is covered under one of those coverages. This coverage applies in addition to any coverage automatically provided for custom parts or equipment under Comprehensive Coverage or Collision Coverage.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-RENTAL REIMBURSEMENT COVERAGE

We will reimburse rental charges incurred when you rent an auto from a rental agency or auto repair shop due to a loss to a covered auto for which Rental Reimbursement Coverage has been purchased. This coverage applies only if you have purchased both Comprehensive Coverage and Collision Coverage for that covered auto and the loss is covered under one of those coverages.

Additional fees or charges for insurance, damage waivers, optional equipment, fuel, or accessories are not covered.

This coverage is limited to the each day limit shown on the declarations page for a maximum of 30 days.

If  Rental Reimbursement Coverage applies, no other coverage under this policy for rental expenses will apply .

## Rental charges will be reimbursed beginning:

- 1 . when the covered auto cannot be driven due to a loss; or
2. if the covered auto can be driven, when you deliver the covered auto to an auto repair shop or one of our Service Centers for repairs due to the loss; and ending the earliest of:
- 1 . when the covered auto has been returned to you ;
2. when the covered auto has been repaired;
3. when the covered auto has been replaced;
4. 72 hours after we make an offer to settle the loss if the covered auto is deemed by us to be a total loss; or
5. when you incur 30 days worth of rental charges.

You must provide us written proof of your rental charges to be reimbursed.

The 'each person' limit of liability includes the total of all claims made for bodily injury to an insured person and all claims of others derived from such bodily injury , including, but not limited to, emotional injury or mental anguish resulting from the bodily injury of another or from witnessing the bodily injury to another, loss of society , loss of companionship, loss of services, loss of consortium, and wrongful death.

If an insured person incurs expenses for medical services that we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary, we may refuse to pay for those expenses and contest them.

The policy offers two primary forms of compensation: reimbursement for veterinary expenses incurred due to injuries sustained in the incident, and a death benefit if the pet dies as a result. The death benefit is capped at $1,000, and this amount is reduced by any veterinary expenses already paid under the policy. Additionally, the total coverage for all damages in a single loss is limited to $1,000, which includes both veterinary costs and the death benefit. This means that if veterinary expenses are paid, they are subtracted from the $1,000 death benefit limit, ensuring the combined payout does not exceed the overall maximum. PET INJURY COVERAGE is intended to offer peace of mind to pet owners by acknowledging the emotional and financial value of their pets in the context of auto insurance. It is important to note that the coverage is contingent upon the pet being inside a covered vehicle at the time of the incident and that the loss must be covered under the primary auto policy. The provision is not intended to replace comprehensive pet insurance but rather to supplement auto insurance with targeted benefits for pet-related losses during vehicle accidents or thefts. By combining veterinary expense reimbursement with a fixed death benefit, PET INJURY COVERAGE provides a structured, limited financial safety net for pet owners facing unexpected losses involving their animals due to auto-related events.|8

## PART IV-DAMAGE TO A VEHICLE

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COLLISION COVERAGE

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to a:

- 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or
2. non-owned auto ;

and its custom parts or equipment , resulting from collision .

In addition, we will pay the reasonable cost to replace any child safety seat damaged in an accident to which this coverage applies.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COMPREHENSIVE COVERAGE

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to a:

- 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or
2. non-owned auto ;

and its custom parts or equipment , that is not caused by collision .

## A loss not caused by collision includes:

- 1 . contact with an animal (including a bird);
2. explosion or earthquake;
3. fire;
4. malicious mischief or vandalism;
5. missiles or falling objects;
6. riot or civil commotion;
- 7 . theft or larceny;
8. windstorm, hail, water or flood; or
9. breakage of glass not caused by collision .

## In addition, we will pay for:

- 1 . reasonable transportation expenses incurred by you if a covered auto is stolen; and
2. loss of use damages that you are legally liable to pay if a non-owned auto is stolen. A combined maximum of $900, not exceeding $30 per day, will apply to these additional benefits. The additional benefit for transportation expenses will not apply if you purchased Rental Reimbursement Coverage for the stolen covered auto .

Coverage for transportation expenses and loss of use damages begins 48 hours after you report the theft to us and ends the earliest of:

- 1 . when the auto has been recovered and returned to you or its owner;
2. when the auto has been recovered and repaired;
3. when the auto has been replaced;
4. 72 hours after we make an offer to settle the loss if the auto is deemed by us to be a total loss; or

5. if the loss is theft of a rented non-owned auto , 30 days after loss of use begins on the loss.

We must receive written proof of transportation expenses and loss of use damages.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-ADDITIONAL CUSTOM PARTS OR EQUIPMENT COVERAGE

We will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to custom parts or equipment on a covered auto for which this coverage has been purchased. This coverage applies only if you have purchased both Comprehensive Coverage and Collision Coverage for that covered auto and the loss is covered under one of those coverages. This coverage applies in addition to any coverage automatically provided for custom parts or equipment under Comprehensive Coverage or Collision Coverage.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-RENTAL REIMBURSEMENT COVERAGE

We will reimburse rental charges incurred when you rent an auto from a rental agency or auto repair shop due to a loss to a covered auto for which Rental Reimbursement Coverage has been purchased. This coverage applies only if you have purchased both Comprehensive Coverage and Collision Coverage for that covered auto and the loss is covered under one of those coverages.

Additional fees or charges for insurance, damage waivers, optional equipment, fuel, or accessories are not covered.

This coverage is limited to the each day limit shown on the declarations page for a maximum of 30 days.

If  Rental Reimbursement Coverage applies, no other coverage under this policy for rental expenses will apply .

## Rental charges will be reimbursed beginning:

- 1 . when the covered auto cannot be driven due to a loss; or
2. if the covered auto can be driven, when you deliver the covered auto to an auto repair shop or one of our Service Centers for repairs due to the loss; and ending the earliest of:
- 1 . when the covered auto has been returned to you ;
2. when the covered auto has been repaired;
3. when the covered auto has been replaced;
4. 72 hours after we make an offer to settle the loss if the covered auto is deemed by us to be a total loss; or
